definition_zh: 社会规范；一个群体共同接受、用来判断行为是否得体的规则
definition_en: a shared rule or expectation within a group about how its members ought to behave
core_image: 村口水井旁没有人维持秩序，后来的人却自动站到队尾，一条看不见的线把众人的动作排成同一顺序
scene: 北方小镇的集市上，摊位前没有人维持秩序，后来的人却自动站到队尾。A social norm keeps the queue orderly even when no guard is present.
sceneCN: 这里 social norm 指群体共同接受、无须明说却约束行为的行为规则（第 1 个义项：共享的行为期待）；句意为一条社会规范让队伍在没有管理员时也保持整齐。

pos.zh: 社会规范；社会准则（可数，指一条具体规范时多用复数）
（社会学）某一群体共享的行为期待与评价标准

derivatives.zh: 规范；准则（由拉丁 norma「曲尺、规则」直接借入，指衡量行为的尺子）
规范的；应然的（由 norm 加表示「倾向」的拉丁后缀构成，转指「应当如何」的评价标准）
正常的；通常的（由 norma 加表示「属于」的拉丁后缀构成，从「合乎尺规」转指「合乎常规」）
使正常化；使标准化（由 normal 加表示「使成为」的后缀构成，转指使某物回到常规状态）
好交际的；合群的（由拉丁 socius「同伴」加表示「能……」的后缀构成，转指易于与人相伴）

senses.title: A shared rule of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 群体共同接受的行为规则
senses.definition: a rule about how people should behave that a group accepts and passes on
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体接受并沿袭的、关于人应当如何行为的规则
senses.example: A social norm keeps the queue orderly even when no guard is present.
senses.exampleCN: 一条社会规范让队伍在没有管理员时也保持整齐。
senses.why: The phrase joins a Latin word for a measuring square to a Latin word for a companion: a norm is the square against which a group measures behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把拉丁语里表示「曲尺」的词接到表示「同伴」的词上：规范就是群体用来量行为的尺子。

senses.title: An expectation backed by disapproval
senses.titleCN: 靠舆论与排斥维持的期待
senses.definition: an expectation whose breach brings frowns, gossip, exclusion or loss of trust rather than legal punishment
senses.definitionCN: 违反后会招来皱眉、闲话、排挤或失去信任，而非法律惩罚的期待
senses.example: Neighbours enforce the social norm by refusing to lend tools to anyone who never returns them.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们用「不借工具给有借无还的人」来执行这条社会规范。
senses.why: The group is the court: enforcement works through approval and withdrawal of approval, not through police.
senses.whyCN: 群体本身就是法庭：执行靠的是赞许与撤回赞许，而不是警察。

senses.title: Descriptive norm: what people actually do
senses.titleCN: 描述性规范：多数人实际怎么做
senses.definition: the behaviour that most members of a group actually perform, which others copy because it looks normal
senses.definitionCN: 群体中多数人实际做出的行为，旁人因为看上去正常而跟着照做
senses.example: Surveys show the descriptive norm is to recycle, even where no rule requires it.
senses.exampleCN: 调查显示，描述性规范是回收，即使没有规则要求。
senses.why: Sociologists split norms into two readings: the average behaviour and the approved behaviour. This sense is the average.
senses.whyCN: 社会学家把规范分成两种读法：多数人的实际行为与多数人赞成的行为。这个义项指前者。

senses.title: Injunctive norm: what people approve of
senses.titleCN: 指令性规范：多数人赞成什么
senses.definition: the behaviour that most members of a group approve or disapprove of, regardless of what they do themselves
senses.definitionCN: 群体中多数人赞成或不赞成的行为，与他们自己是否照做无关
senses.example: The injunctive norm says littering is wrong, yet many who say so still drop wrappers.
senses.exampleCN: 指令性规范认为乱扔垃圾不对，可许多这样说的人自己仍会丢包装纸。
senses.why: Approval is a separate track from practice: what people praise and what people do can pull in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 赞许与实行是两条轨道：人们称赞什么，与人们实际做什么，可能朝相反方向拉。

senses.title: An internalized obligation
senses.titleCN: 内化为个人义务的规范
senses.definition: a norm a person has absorbed so deeply that breaking it feels like personal guilt rather than public risk
senses.definitionCN: 一个人吸收得极深的规范，违反时感觉像个人愧疚，而不是怕被人看见
senses.example: She felt a pang of guilt for interrupting, so strong was the internalized norm.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为打断别人而感到一阵愧疚，这条内化的规范强到这种程度。
senses.why: Once the group's gaze moves inside the person, enforcement no longer needs witnesses.
senses.whyCN: 当群体的目光移进人的内心，执行就不再需要见证者。

senses.title: A formalized institutional standard
senses.titleCN: 制度化、成文化的行为标准
senses.definition: a norm written into the rules of a school, profession or organization and enforced by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 写进学校、行业或组织规则、由权威执行的规范
senses.example: The hospital turned courtesy into a formal social norm with a written code.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院把礼貌变成一条配有成文守则的正式社会规范。
senses.why: Institutions stabilize norms by writing them down, adding a sanction and a person whose job is to apply it.
senses.whyCN: 机构把规范写下来，再补上处罚与专门执行的人，规范因此稳定下来。

senses.title: A statistical regularity
senses.definition: the most common pattern in a set of observations, used as a baseline for judging what is unusual
senses.definitionCN: 一组观察中最常见的模式，用来判断什么算异常
senses.example: The study treated the social norm as the average number of children per household.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把每户平均子女数当作社会常规。
senses.why: Statistics borrows the word because an average is also a rule: it tells you what to expect before you look.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用这个词，因为平均值也是一条规则：它在你观察之前就告诉你该期待什么。

senses.title: Abstract: any standard of correctness
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何正确性标准
senses.definition: any standard, explicit or implicit, by which a group decides that something is right or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 群体用来判定某事正确或可接受的任何标准，无论明说还是默认
senses.example: Every discipline develops its own social norm of what counts as a good question.
senses.exampleCN: 每门学科都会形成自己的社会规范，界定什么样的问题算好问题。
senses.why: At its widest the phrase means the measuring stick itself, apart from who holds it or what it measures.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个短语指的就是那把尺子本身，与谁拿着它、量什么都无关。

intro.en: The phrase couples Latin norma, a carpenter's measuring square, with socialis, 'of companions'. Its sociological sense is about a century old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语 norma（木匠的曲尺）与 socialis（同伴的）接在一起；它的社会学义大约只有一百年历史。年代均为约数。

items.en: Norma meant 'carpenter's square, rule, pattern'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a connection with Greek gnomon 'pointer on a sundial' has been suggested but is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: norma 意为「木匠的曲尺、规则、范型」。它更深的来源不确定；有人提出它与希腊语 gnomon「日晷指针」有关，但那只是假说。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally'. It is generally traced to Latin sequi 'to follow', from a reconstructed Indo-European root meaning 'to follow'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。一般认为它可追溯到拉丁语 sequi「跟随」，其印欧词根为重构形式，意为「跟随」。

items.en: Socialis 'of companionship, of allies' gave French social and English social; the adjective names what is shared among companions.
items.cn: socialis「同伴的、盟友的」衍生法语 social 与英语 social；这个形容词指同伴之间共享的东西。

items.en: Social entered English in the sixteenth century. Norm followed much later as a learned borrowing from Latin, first as a rule or pattern in general.
items.cn: social 在十六世纪进入英语。norm 晚得多才作为学术借词从拉丁语进入，最初泛指规则或范型。

items.en: In early twentieth-century sociology norm narrowed to a standard of behaviour shared by a group, and social norm became a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 在二十世纪初的社会学中，norm 收窄为群体共享的行为标准，social norm 也随之成为固定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded, the link between norma and gnomon is unproven, and the Indo-European root behind sequi is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：完整短语最早印行于何时没有记录；norma 与 gnomon 的联系未获证明；sequi 背后的印欧词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates the measuring square from words that only look or sound close; group two holds the neighbours that also guide behaviour.
note.cn: 第一组把这个「曲尺」与只是形近或音近的词分开；第二组是同样引导行为的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The rule itself, without the group. It can be a standard of behaviour or a statistical average; the full phrase adds the shared, group-wide dimension.
entries.definitionCN: 规则本身，不含群体这一层；它可以是行为标准，也可以是统计平均值，而完整短语补上了群体共享的维度。

entries.definition: Built on norma plus an adjective ending: conforming to a standard, hence ordinary. A normal act is not necessarily a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 由 norma 加形容词后缀构成：合乎标准，因而寻常；一个正常的行为不一定是规范。

entries.definition: From Latin enormis 'out of rule', literally the prefix for 'out' plus norma. It looks unrelated but shares the measuring-square root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 enormis「出了规矩」，字面是表示「向外」的前缀加 norma；看似无关，却同出「曲尺」词根。

entries.definition: From Latin forma 'shape, mould', not norma. It looks and sounds close but carries no rule sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 forma「形状、模子」，并非 norma；形音都近，却没有规则义。

entries.definition: An agreed practice, often explicit and formal; a norm can be unwritten and enforced only by disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 经约定形成的做法，往往明确而正式；规范可以不成文，只靠不赞许来执行。

entries.definition: A traditional way of doing something, handed down over time; it is usually older and more local than a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 世代沿袭的做法；通常比规范更古老、更具地方性。

entries.definition: The moral norms of a society, felt as strong and sacred; a norm can be merely procedural.
entries.definitionCN: 一个社会被视作强烈而神圣的道德规范；而规范可以只是程序性的。

entries.definition: An explicit instruction, as in a game or a school; a norm may never be written down.
entries.definitionCN: 明确的指令，如游戏或学校中的规定；规范则可能从不落成文字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, so a norm is the square a group holds against your behaviour.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，所以 norm 就是群体拿来量你行为的那把尺。

normal.en: Socius meant companion, so the full phrase is the rule companions share.
normal.cn: socius 意为同伴，所以这个完整说法就是同伴之间共享的规则。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the force: follow a norm, violate a norm, enforce a norm.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示约束力：遵守规范、违反规范、执行规范。

normal.en: Descriptive and injunctive are the two sociological readings: what people do and what people approve.
normal.cn: 描述性与指令性是两种社会学读法：人们实际怎么做，与人们赞成什么。

normal.en: The derived words keep the measuring idea: normative, normal, normalize.
normal.cn: 派生词保留「测量」的意象：规范的、正常的、使标准化。

abstract.en: Picture a queue forming without a sign, each newcomer reading the backs of the others.
abstract.cn: 想象队伍在没有标牌时自己形成，每个后来者都在读前面人的背影。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone lowers their voice at dusk without being told.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，黄昏时所有人不用谁提醒就压低声音。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler passed hand to hand, never seen, yet every hand measures by it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子被一只手递给另一只手，谁也看不见它，却都拿它来量。

examples.en: The village keeps the social norm that tools are returned the same evening.
examples.cn: 村里守着一条社会规范：工具当晚归还。

examples.en: Breaking a social norm can cost more trust than breaking a written rule.
examples.cn: 违反一条社会规范，失去的信任可能比违反一条成文规则更多。

examples.en: Sociologists distinguish the descriptive norm from the injunctive norm.
examples.cn: 社会学家把描述性规范与指令性规范区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜秀 诺姆」——社会同伴手里那把量行为的曲尺 → 社会规范

root: 拉丁 norma「木匠的曲尺、规则」+ 拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」；norma 更深来源不确定，socius 一般认为与 sequi「跟随」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the group's shared expectation to the two ways sociologists measure it, then inward to guilt, outward to written rules, and finally to the measuring stick itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从群体共享的期待出发，转到社会学家测量它的两种方式，再向内变成愧疚、向外变成成文规则，最后落到那把尺子本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group holds an invisible measuring square and quietly checks every member against it.
core.cn: 核心意象：群体握着一把看不见的曲尺，悄悄把每个成员对照它量一遍。

branches.en: THE GROUP AS COURT: a shared rule plus the approval and disapproval that enforce it.
branches.cn: 群体即法庭：共享的规则，加上执行它的赞许与不赞许。

branches.en: TWO READINGS: what members actually do versus what members approve of.
branches.cn: 两种读法：成员实际怎么做，对比成员赞成什么。

branches.en: INSIDE THE PERSON: the gaze is internalized, so guilt replaces witnesses.
branches.cn: 目光进入内心：规范被内化，愧疚取代了见证者。

branches.en: ON PAPER: institutions write the rule down and attach a sanction.
branches.cn: 落到纸上：机构把规则写下，并配上处罚。

branches.en: THE MEASURING STICK ITSELF: first a statistical average, then any standard of correctness.
branches.cn: 尺子本身：先指统计平均值，再指任何正确性标准。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin stems, each of which also supports a small English family, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁词干构成，每个词干还支撑起一个小型英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma gives norm, normal and enormous; Latin socius gives social, society and sociable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 norma 衍生 norm、normal 与 enormous；拉丁 socius 衍生 social、society 与 sociable。

items.example: The root supplies the image of measurement.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「测量」的意象。

items.example: The root supplies the group.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「群体」这一层。

items.structure: socialis (of companions) through Old French to English
items.example: Social names what is shared among companions.
items.exampleCN: social 指同伴之间共享的东西。

items.example: Norm entered English as a learned word.
items.exampleCN: norm 作为学术词进入英语。

items.example: A normal reading is aligned with the square.
items.exampleCN: 正常的读法就是与曲尺对齐。

items.structure: norm plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'
items.example: Normative talk says what ought to be.
items.exampleCN: 规范性话语说的是「应当如何」。

items.example: Normalize turns a deviation back to the rule.
items.exampleCN: 使标准化就是把偏离拨回规则。

items.structure: socius plus a suffix of state or body
items.example: Society is the whole body of companions.
items.exampleCN: 社会就是同伴构成的整体。

items.meaningCN: 出了规矩的；因而巨大的
items.example: Enormous began as 'outside the square'.
items.exampleCN: enormous 最初意为「在曲尺之外」。

definition_zh: 价值；价格；重要性；复数指价值观；动词指重视或估价
definition_en: the worth, importance or monetary price of something, or to regard something as important
core_image: 集市上有人把一枚旧铜钱放在掌心反复掂量，一边看成色，一边想它对自己意味着什么
scene: 旧货摊前，摊主把一只缺口的瓷碗翻过来，先看底款，再想它值多少钱。She tried to value the chipped bowl before naming a price.
sceneCN: 这里 value 指给某物估定价格（第 8 个义项：估量货币价值）；句意为她在开价之前先试着估算这只缺口瓷碗值多少钱。

pos.zh: 价值；价格；重要性（不可数，指抽象价值时不可数）
价值观；价值准则（多用复数 values）
重视；珍视；估价；给……定价

derivatives.zh: 贵重的；有价值的（由 value 加表示「能……」的后缀构成，转指值得付出代价）
估价；估值（由 value 加表示「动作结果」的后缀构成，转指估定价值的过程或结果）
评价；评估（由表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 value 的词根构成，转指把价值算出来）
英勇（由拉丁 valere「强健」加表示「性质」的后缀构成，转指精神上的强）
有效的；有根据的（由拉丁 valere「有力」加表示「具有」的后缀构成，转指站得住）

senses.title: Monetary worth
senses.definition: the amount of money that something can be sold for or is worth in exchange
senses.definitionCN: 某物可以卖得的钱数，或它在交换中值多少
senses.example: The value of the old house doubled after the road was paved.
senses.exampleCN: 道路铺好后，这栋老房子的价值翻了一倍。
senses.why: The oldest economic sense: value is what a thing will fetch when it changes hands.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的经济义：价值就是一件东西转手时能换到的东西。

senses.title: Usefulness or importance
senses.definition: the importance or usefulness of something for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 某物对某个目的而言的重要程度或有用程度
senses.example: Scholars still debate the value of the manuscript to historians.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们仍在争论这份手稿对历史学家的价值。
senses.why: Here the measure is not money but benefit: a thing is valuable because it helps someone do something.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度不是钱，而是益处：一件东西有价值，是因为它能帮人做成某事。

senses.title: A moral principle
senses.definition: a belief about what is right or important, usually used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 关于什么是对或重要的信念，通常用复数
senses.example: The school lists honesty and respect among its core values.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校把诚实与尊重列为核心价值。
senses.why: A person's values are the standards by which they rank goods, so the word moves from price to principle.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的价值观就是他排序各种善好的标准，词义于是从价格移到原则。

senses.title: Lightness of a colour
senses.definition: the degree of lightness or darkness of a colour, from black to white
senses.definitionCN: 一种颜色由黑到白的明暗程度
senses.example: The painter adjusted the value of the blue until the sky receded.
senses.exampleCN: 画家调整蓝色的明度，直到天空退到远处。
senses.why: Painters borrowed the economic word for a scale: each tone is worth more or less light.
senses.whyCN: 画家借用这个经济词来表示刻度：每个色调值多少光。

senses.title: A number assigned in mathematics
senses.definition: the number or amount assigned to a variable or expression
senses.definitionCN: 赋予变量或表达式的数或量
senses.example: Substitute three for x and the value of the expression becomes eleven.
senses.exampleCN: 把 x 代入三，这个表达式的值就变成十一。
senses.why: Mathematics keeps only the idea of an assigned amount, stripped of price and preference.
senses.whyCN: 数学只保留「被赋予的量」这一层，剥去价格与偏好。

senses.title: Duration of a note
senses.definition: the length of a note or rest, measured in beats
senses.definitionCN: 音符或休止符的长度，以拍计算
senses.example: A dotted note has one and a half times the value of the plain note.
senses.exampleCN: 附点音符的时值是普通音符的一倍半。
senses.why: A note's worth is measured in time, so the same word serves a second technical scale.
senses.whyCN: 音符的「价值」以时间衡量，于是同一个词服务第二种技术刻度。

senses.title: To regard highly
senses.definition: to regard someone or something as important and worthy of care
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物看得重要、值得照料
senses.example: She values her neighbours' advice more than any handbook.
senses.exampleCN: 她看重邻居的建议，胜过任何手册。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of asking what a thing is worth, it says that you assign worth to it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来：不再问一件东西值多少，而是说你把它看得有价值。

senses.title: To estimate a price
senses.definition: to estimate the monetary worth of something, often professionally
senses.definitionCN: 估算某物的货币价值，常指专业估价
senses.example: She tried to value the chipped bowl before naming a price.
senses.exampleCN: 她在开价之前先试着估算这只缺口瓷碗值多少钱。
senses.why: This is the oldest verb use: to set a price, literally to put a value on.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的动词用法：定出价格，字面上就是「把价值放上去」。

senses.title: Abstract: worthwhileness
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：值得追求的性质
senses.definition: the quality that makes something worth wanting, doing or preserving
senses.definitionCN: 使某物值得想要、去做或保存的性质
senses.example: The novel's value lies in the questions it leaves open.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的价值在于它留下的问题。
senses.why: At its widest, value is not a number but a reason: it answers why anything should matter.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，价值不是一个数，而是一个理由：它回答为什么某事物值得在意。

intro.en: Value comes through Old French from Latin valere 'to be strong, be worth'. The noun first named price, then importance, then moral standards and technical scales. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: value 经古法语来自拉丁 valere「强健、有价值」。这个名词先指价格，再指重要性，随后扩展到道德标准与技术刻度。年代均为约数。

items.en: Valere meant 'to be strong, to be well, to be worth'. The sense of worth grew out of the idea of having force or power.
items.cn: valere 意为「强健、安好、有价值」。价值义从「有力量」这一层长出来。

items.en: The root behind valere is usually reconstructed as a Indo-European form meaning 'to be strong'. This is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: valere 背后的词根通常被重构为一个意为「强健」的印欧形式。这是重构形式，并非有文献记录的词。

items.en: Old French value, the feminine past participle of valoir 'to be worth', carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 value 是 valoir「值」的阴性过去分词，在十四世纪把这个名词带进英语。

items.en: English value first meant 'worth, price'. The plural values as a name for moral beliefs is much later and belongs to modern social language.
items.cn: 英语 value 最初意为「价值、价格」。复数 values 用来指道德信念要晚得多，属于现代社会科学语言。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries values became a standard term for shared moral beliefs, especially in sociology and education.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，values 成为指共享道德信念的标准术语，尤其用于社会学与教育学。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and deeper origin): the exact first use of values in the moral sense is not recorded, and the Indo-European root of valere is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：values 的 moral 义最早用于何时没有记录；valere 的印欧词根属重构形式，并非有文献记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin 'be strong' root together with one look-alike from a different root; group two holds the near meanings of worth.
note.cn: 第一组把同出拉丁「强健」词根的词与一个异源形近词放在一起；第二组是「价值」的邻近意思。

entries.definition: From Latin valor 'worth, bravery', built on valere. It names personal courage, not price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 valor「价值、勇敢」，由 valere 构成；它指个人勇气，不指价格。

entries.definition: From Latin validus 'strong', also from valere. It means legally or logically sound, not valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 validus「强壮的」，同出 valere；它指法律或逻辑上站得住，而非有价值。

entries.definition: The verb for assessing worth or performance; value can also be a verb, but evaluate is the technical one.
entries.definitionCN: 评估价值或表现的动词；value 也可作动词，但 evaluate 更技术化。

entries.definition: From Old French valee and Latin vallis 'valley'. It shares letters and sound with value but has no worth sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 valee 与拉丁 vallis「山谷」；与 value 形音相近，却无价值义。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for how much something deserves; value is more formal and often economic.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某物应得多少的日常名词；value 更正式，且常带经济色彩。

entries.definition: The money asked or paid for a thing; value is what it is judged to be worth, which may differ.
entries.definitionCN: 卖方要价或买方付的钱；value 是判断它值多少，两者可能不同。

entries.definition: The quality of deserving reward or praise, usually of a person or an action.
entries.definitionCN: 应得奖励或赞扬的品质，通常用于人或行为。

entries.definition: The weight something carries in a situation; value adds the idea of worth, not only influence.
entries.definitionCN: 某物在情境中的分量；value 还带有「值得」的意思，不只是影响力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Valere meant to be strong, so value is the force a thing has when it is weighed.
normal.cn: valere 意为强健，所以 value 就是一件东西被掂量时具有的分量。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: market value, sentimental value, value for money.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：市场价值、情感价值、性价比。

normal.en: Values in the plural usually means moral beliefs, not prices.
normal.cn: 复数的 values 通常指道德信念，而不是价格。

normal.en: The verb has two directions: value a friend means regard, value a house means price.
normal.cn: 动词有两个方向：看重朋友是重视，给房子估价是定价。

normal.en: Technical scales borrow the word: colour value and note value.
normal.cn: 技术刻度也借用这个词：色彩明度与音符时值。

abstract.en: Picture a hand weighing a coin, then weighing a friendship, then weighing a colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手先掂钱币，再掂一段情谊，再掂一块颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag that keeps being rewritten as different people look at the same object.
abstract.cn: 想象同一件东西被不同人看时，价签被一次次改写。

abstract.en: Picture a note held longer than written, so its worth grows in time rather than money.
abstract.cn: 想象一个音符被拖得比谱面更长，它的价值在时间里而不是在钱里增长。

examples.en: Rising rents changed the value of the shop.
examples.cn: 租金上涨改变了这间店铺的价值。

examples.en: Her parents taught her the value of keeping promises.
examples.cn: 她的父母教她守信的价值。

examples.en: The violin's value to the family was sentimental, not financial.
examples.cn: 这把小提琴对这家人是情感价值，而非金钱价值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瓦尔优」——把东西放上天平量一量 → 价值、重视

root: 拉丁 valere「强健、有价值」，经古法语 value 进入英语；其印欧词根为重构形式，非有文献记录的形态。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one gesture of weighing and send it to money, usefulness, moral beliefs, colour, mathematics, music, regard, pricing and finally to worthwhileness itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保留同一个「掂量」动作，再把它送到金钱、用处、道德信念、色彩、数学、音乐、重视、定价，最后送到「值得」本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand weighs a coin, a friendship and a patch of colour with the same movement.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手用同一个动作掂钱币、掂情谊、掂一块颜色。

branches.en: PRICE AND ESTIMATE: the noun names what a thing fetches, and the oldest verb sets that figure.
branches.cn: 价格与估价：名词指一件东西能换到什么，最古老的动词则把这个数目定下来。

branches.en: ASSIGNED AMOUNT: usefulness is benefit, and mathematics keeps only the assigned number.
branches.cn: 被赋予的量：用处是益处，数学只保留被赋予的数。

branches.en: FROM PRINCIPLE TO REASON: shared moral standards, then whatever makes anything matter.
branches.cn: 从原则到理由：先是共享的道德标准，再是使任何事物值得在意的性质。

branches.en: TECHNICAL SCALES: colour is measured by light and music by time.
branches.cn: 技术刻度：颜色以光衡量，音乐以时间衡量。

branches.en: REGARD: the verb that assigns worth to a person or thing.
branches.cn: 重视：把价值赋予某人或某物的动词。

intro.en: Value is a Latin verb root that English turned into a noun, a verb and a family of measuring words.
intro.cn: value 是一个拉丁动词词根，英语把它变成名词、动词以及一组成熟的测量词。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere gives value, valid, valour and evaluate; the same root underlies valentia 'strength'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 valere 衍生 value、valid、valour 与 evaluate；同一词根还构成 valentia「力量」。

items.meaning: to be strong, be well, be worth
items.example: The root carries strength and worth at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时带着力量与价值。

items.example: The noun and verb share one root.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词共享一个词根。

items.structure: value plus a suffix meaning 'able to be'
items.example: A valuable thing can bear a price.
items.exampleCN: 有价值的东西经得起估价。

items.example: The negative form denies worth altogether.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式把价值整体取消。

items.structure: value plus a suffix of action or result
items.meaning: the act or result of pricing
items.example: Valuation is the noun of the pricing act.
items.exampleCN: 估值就是定价动作的名词。

items.structure: an outward prefix plus the value root
items.meaning: to work out the worth of something
items.example: Evaluate calculates worth rather than feeling it.
items.exampleCN: 评估是把价值算出来，而不是感受它。

items.example: Valid keeps the 'strength' side of the root.
items.exampleCN: valid 保留了词根里「有力」的一面。

items.structure: valere plus a suffix of quality
items.example: Valour is strength of a person, not of a price.
items.exampleCN: 英勇是人的强，而不是价格的强。

items.structure: valid plus a suffix of state
items.example: Validity is the state of standing up.
items.exampleCN: 有效性就是站得住的状态。

latinEntries.meaning: to be strong; to be worth

definition_zh: 社会价值；某一事物对群体福祉与社会关系所具有的价值；也指社会共同认可的价值观
definition_en: the worth that something has for a community's wellbeing and relationships, or the values a society shares
core_image: 一条修好的村道通向学校，孩子们少走半小时，账本上却没有这笔收益，价值落在人身上而不落在钱包里
scene: 社区把废弃仓库改成公共厨房，志愿者计算它能给邻里带来多少好处。The group measured the social value of turning the empty warehouse into a shared kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 social value 指一项安排给社区带来的整体好处（第 1 个义项：对群体福祉的净益处）；句意为这个团体评估把空仓库改成公共厨房能带来多少社会价值。

pos.zh: 社会价值；社会效益（多作不可数，指对群体的整体好处）
社会价值观（用复数 social values，指一个社会共同认可的价值准则）

forms.label: 复数（指多种价值或价值准则）

derivatives.zh: 社会的；社交的（由拉丁 socius「同伴」加表示「属于」的后缀构成，转指属于同伴群体）
社会层面的（由 society 加表示「属于」的后缀构成，转指整个社会层面而非个人）
价值；重视（由拉丁 valere「强健、有价值」经古法语进入英语）
有价值的；贵重的（由 value 加表示「能……」的后缀构成，转指值得付出代价）
估价；估值（由 value 加表示「动作结果」的后缀构成，转指估定价值的过程或结果）
评估；评价（由表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 value 的词根构成，转指把价值算出来）

senses.title: Net benefit to a community
senses.definition: the overall benefit that something brings to a community, including effects that no market price captures
senses.definitionCN: 某事物给一个共同体带来的整体好处，包括市场价格计不进去的效果
senses.example: The group measured the social value of turning the empty warehouse into a shared kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团体评估把空仓库改成公共厨房能带来多少社会价值。
senses.why: The phrase takes the economic noun and widens its measure from buyers to a whole community.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把经济名词的尺度从买家扩展到整个共同体。

senses.title: Shared moral values
senses.definition: the beliefs about right and good that a society holds in common, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会共同持有的、关于对与善的信念，通常用复数
senses.example: Debates over taxation often turn into arguments about social values.
senses.exampleCN: 关于税收的争论常常变成关于社会价值观的争论。
senses.why: Here the word is not benefit but principle: what a society agrees to prize.
senses.whyCN: 这里谈的不是益处，而是原则：一个社会一致珍视什么。

senses.title: Social return on investment
senses.definition: the social and environmental return produced by an investment, often compared with its financial return
senses.definitionCN: 一项投资产生的社会与环境回报，常与财务回报并列计算
senses.example: The fund reports a social value of three pounds for every pound spent.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金报告每投入一英镑产生三英镑的社会价值。
senses.why: Accountants borrowed the word so that benefits to people could be put beside benefits to shareholders.
senses.whyCN: 会计行业借用这个词，使对人的益处能与对股东的益处并列。

senses.title: Symbolic value in consumption
senses.titleCN: 消费中的社会象征价值
senses.definition: the social meaning a good carries, such as status, belonging or taste, beyond its practical use
senses.definitionCN: 商品承载的社会含义，如地位、归属或品味，超出实用之外
senses.example: The brand's social value lay in the kind of crowd it let buyers join.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的社会价值在于它让买家加入哪一类人群。
senses.why: Sociology of consumption added this sense: objects are bought for what they say about the buyer.
senses.whyCN: 消费社会学加入这一义项：人买东西，也为了它替买家说了什么。

senses.title: Value of social ties
senses.definition: the worth of relationships, trust and networks, often measured as social capital
senses.definitionCN: 关系、信任与网络所具有的价值，常以社会资本衡量
senses.example: Neighbours who watch each other's homes create social value that insurance cannot replace.
senses.exampleCN: 互相照看房屋的邻居创造了保险无法替代的社会价值。
senses.why: Relationships are a resource, so the phrase can name the worth stored in a network.
senses.whyCN: 关系本身就是资源，因此这个短语可以指储存在网络里的价值。

senses.title: Collective preference in economics
senses.definition: the value that a group assigns to a good, as distinct from the summed preferences of individuals
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体赋予某物的价值，区别于个体偏好的简单加总
senses.example: Welfare economics asks whether a policy increases social value overall.
senses.exampleCN: 福利经济学追问一项政策是否整体上增加了社会价值。
senses.why: Once choices are aggregated, the group's value need not equal any individual's value.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把选择加总，群体的价值就不必等于任何个人的价值。

senses.title: Social value in public policy
senses.titleCN: 公共政策中的社会价值
senses.definition: the social outcomes that public bodies require from procurement, funding or regulation
senses.definitionCN: 公共机构要求采购、资助或监管所产生的社会结果
senses.example: The council now scores bids partly on social value, such as local hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会如今部分按社会价值给投标打分，例如本地用工。
senses.why: Policy turned the phrase into an award criterion, so it names outcomes a contract must deliver.
senses.whyCN: 政策把这个短语变成评标标准，于是它指合同必须交付的社会结果。

senses.title: Abstract: worth measured by effect on people
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：以对人的影响衡量的价值
senses.definition: any worth judged by how it affects people's lives rather than by what it sells for
senses.definitionCN: 任何以对人们生活的影响而非售价来判定的价值
senses.example: A library's social value shows in who feels welcome, not in its ticket sales.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的社会价值体现在谁觉得自己受欢迎，而不在门票收入。
senses.why: At its widest the phrase asks what a thing does for people, setting that against what it costs.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个短语问的是一件事为人做了什么，再把它与代价对照。

intro.en: The phrase joins social, from Latin socius 'companion', to value, from Latin valere 'be worth'. It became a measure in economics and later in policy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自拉丁 socius「同伴」的 social 与来自拉丁 valere「有价值」的 value 接在一起。它先成为经济学的衡量词，后来进入政策语言。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally' and gives social, society and sociable through Latin socialis.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」，经拉丁 socialis 衍生 social、society 与 sociable。

items.en: Valere meant 'to be strong, be worth' and gives value, valid and valour.
items.cn: valere 意为「强健、有价值」，衍生 value、valid 与 valour。

items.en: Both nouns entered English through Old French: social in the sixteenth century, value in the fourteenth. The compound phrase is later than either word.
items.cn: 两个名词都经古法语进入英语：social 在十六世纪，value 在十四世纪。合成短语比这两个词都晚。

items.en: Nineteenth-century political economy used social value for worth judged by its effect on the community rather than by individual exchange.
items.cn: 十九世纪的政治经济学用 social value 指按对共同体的效果而非个人交换来判定的价值。

items.en: In the late twentieth century the phrase became a criterion in procurement, social investment and corporate reporting.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，这个短语成为公共采购、社会投资与企业报告中的一项标准。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first printed use of the exact compound is not recorded, and the senses in economics and policy overlap in the record.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个确切合成短语最早印行于何时没有记录，经济学与政策中的两个义项在文献里彼此交叠。

note.en: Group one separates the compound from its plural moral sense and from neighbouring measures; group two holds broader ideas of public worth.
note.cn: 第一组把这个合成短语与它的复数道德义、以及邻近的衡量概念分开；第二组是更宽泛的公共价值概念。

entries.definition: The plural normally names the moral beliefs a society holds, not a measured benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 复数通常指一个社会持有的道德信念，而不是可衡量的益处。

entries.definition: A plainer phrase for how much a person or thing matters to others; it lacks the economic and policy edge.
entries.definitionCN: 更朴素的说法，指某人或某物对他人有多重要；它没有经济与政策的锋利边缘。

entries.definition: A management term for policies that profit the company and the community at once; it is a strategy label, not a general measure.
entries.definitionCN: 一个管理术语，指同时让公司与社区受益的政策；它是策略标签，不是一般衡量。

entries.definition: The trust and networks a community can draw on; it is one source of social value, not the value itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一个共同体可动用的信任与网络；它是社会价值的一个来源，而非价值本身。

entries.definition: The worth that public services create for citizens; it is the policy cousin of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 公共服务为公民创造的价值；它是这个短语在政策领域的近亲。

entries.definition: The change an action produces in people's lives; impact is the effect, social value is the judgement that the effect is good.
entries.definitionCN: 一个行动在人们生活中造成的变化；impact 是效果，social value 则是判定该效果为好。

entries.definition: What benefits everyone in a society; it is a moral ideal rather than a measurable return.
entries.definitionCN: 对一个社会中所有人都有益的东西；它是道德理想，而非可计算的回报。

entries.definition: The wellbeing of people, often measured by income, health and security; it is the outcome social value is claimed to raise.
entries.definitionCN: 人们的福祉，常以收入、健康与安全感衡量；它正是社会价值所声称要提升的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real policy terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的政策术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Social carries the companion root, so the phrase begins with what people share.
normal.cn: social 带着「同伴」词根，所以这个短语从人们共享的东西开始。

normal.en: Value carries the 'be worth' root, so the second half asks what the shared thing is worth.
normal.cn: value 带着「有价值」词根，所以后半段问这件共享之物值多少。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the measure: create social value, measure social value, social value creation.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示衡量动作：创造社会价值、衡量社会价值、社会价值创造。

normal.en: The plural social values shifts to moral beliefs, while the singular usually stays with benefit.
normal.cn: 复数的 social values 转向道德信念，单数通常仍指益处。

normal.en: Policy uses the phrase as a scoring criterion, as in social value in procurement.
normal.cn: 政策把这个短语当作评分标准，如采购中的社会价值。

abstract.en: Picture a repaired footpath that saves children half an hour, though no ledger records the saving.
abstract.cn: 想象一条修好的小路让孩子省下半小时，而账本上不记这笔收益。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse turned into a kitchen where neighbours cook and talk.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库变成厨房，邻居在里面做饭、说话。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag that leaves out the people who benefit.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，把受益的人全部漏掉。

examples.en: The charity reports the social value of its training programme in hours of work gained.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构用获得的工时来报告其培训项目的社会价值。

examples.en: Residents argued that the new road had social value beyond its traffic figures.
examples.cn: 居民认为新路的价值不止交通数字，还有社会价值。

examples.en: The report set social value against the financial cost of the scheme.
examples.cn: 报告把该方案的社会价值与财务成本对照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜秀 瓦尔优」——社会同伴共享的那份值得 → 社会价值

root: 拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」+ 拉丁 valere「强健、有价值」；两个词干分别经古法语进入英语，合成短语晚于两者。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one question, what a thing does for people, and ask it of community benefit, shared beliefs, investment return, status, relationships, collective choice, public contracts and finally any effect on lives.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守住同一个问题——一件事为人做了什么——再依次问向社区益处、共享信念、投资回报、身份、关系、集体选择、公共合同，最后问向任何对人的生活影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a footpath that saves children half an hour sits beside a ledger that records no profit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条让孩子省下半小时的小路，旁边是一本不记这项收益的账。

branches.en: MEASURED BENEFIT: community gain and its accounting cousin, social return on investment.
branches.cn: 可衡量的益处：社区所得，以及它在会计里的近亲——社会投资回报。

branches.en: SHARED BELIEFS AND AGGREGATED CHOICE: what a society prizes, and what a group's summed preference values.
branches.cn: 共享信念与加总选择：一个社会珍视什么，以及一个群体加总偏好后看重什么。

branches.en: SYMBOL AND NETWORK: goods carry standing, and relationships carry stored worth.
branches.cn: 符号与网络：商品承载身份，关系储存价值。

branches.en: CONTRACT CRITERION: policy turns the phrase into an outcome a bid must deliver.
branches.cn: 合同标准：政策把这个短语变成投标必须交付的结果。

branches.en: EFFECT ON LIVES: the widest reading asks only what a thing does for people.
branches.cn: 对人的生活影响：最宽的读法只问一件事为人做了什么。

intro.en: The phrase joins two Latin stems, one naming companions and one naming worth, each with its own English family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把两个拉丁词干接在一起，一个命名同伴，一个命名价值，各自带有一支英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius gives social, society and sociable; Latin valere gives value, valid, valour and evaluate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 social、society 与 sociable；拉丁 valere 衍生 value、valid、valour 与 evaluate。

items.example: The first half names the group.
items.exampleCN: 前半段命名群体。

items.example: Socialis became English social.
items.exampleCN: socialis 成为英语 social。

items.structure: socius plus a suffix of body or state
items.example: Society is the group as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 社会就是作为整体的群体。

items.example: The second half names worth.
items.exampleCN: 后半段命名价值。

items.example: Value turned the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: value 把这个动词变成名词。

items.structure: value plus a suffix meaning 'able to be'
items.example: Valuable is value made an adjective.
items.exampleCN: valuable 是 value 的形容词化。

items.structure: value plus a suffix of action or result
items.example: Valuation names the measuring act.
items.exampleCN: valuation 命名衡量动作。

items.example: Societal lifts the view from persons to a society.
items.exampleCN: societal 把视角从个人抬到社会。

items.structure: an outward prefix plus the value root
items.example: Evaluate calculates social value.
items.exampleCN: evaluate 把社会价值算出来。

definition_zh: 文化规范；某一文化群体共同接受的行为准则与期待
definition_en: a shared expectation within a culture about how people should act
core_image: 进门先脱鞋、吃饭等长辈先动筷，同一间屋子里几代人不用商量就照着做
scene: 沿海渔村，客人进门先把鞋放在门边，主人不用提醒。A cultural norm quietly decides where guests leave their shoes at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural norm 指某一文化群体共同接受的行为准则（第 1 个义项：文化内部共享的期待）；句意为一条文化规范在无人提醒时决定了客人把鞋放在门边。

pos.zh: 文化规范；文化准则（可数，指一条具体规范时多用复数）
某一文化内部关于礼节与分寸的共享标准

derivatives.zh: 文化（由拉丁 cultura「耕作、培养」直接借入，从照料土地转指照料人的心智与习俗）
文化的（由 culture 加表示「属于」的后缀构成，转指属于某一文化）
从文化角度看（由 cultural 加表示「方式」的后缀构成，转指以文化为尺度）
耕作；培养（由拉丁 cultura 的动词词干构成，从照料土地转指照料能力）
规范；准则（由拉丁 norma「曲尺」借入，指衡量行为的尺子）
规范的；应然的（由 norm 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指「应当如何」）

senses.title: A shared expectation within a culture
senses.definition: a rule about behaviour that members of a culture accept without it being written down
senses.definitionCN: 某一文化成员无须明文规定就共同接受的行为规则
senses.example: A cultural norm quietly decides where guests leave their shoes at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一条文化规范在无人提醒时决定了客人把鞋放在门边。
senses.why: Culture names a whole way of life, so its norms are the expectations that hold that way of life together.
senses.whyCN: 文化指一整套生活方式，文化规范就是把这种生活方式拢在一起的期待。

senses.title: A custom handed down
senses.definition: a way of doing something passed from older members to younger ones over generations
senses.definitionCN: 由年长者传给年轻者、沿续数代的做法
senses.example: The cultural norm of eating together at the new year survives in many migrant families.
senses.exampleCN: 新年一起吃饭的文化规范在许多移民家庭里延续下来。
senses.why: What begins as a norm can harden into a custom once repetition turns expectation into inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 当重复把期待变成继承，原本的规范就会固化为习俗。

senses.title: A culture-specific politeness rule
senses.titleCN: 某一文化特有的礼貌规则
senses.definition: a rule of courtesy that is normal in one culture and may seem odd or rude in another
senses.definitionCN: 在一种文化里正常、在另一种文化里可能显得奇怪甚至失礼的礼节规则
senses.example: Removing your shoes indoors is a cultural norm in some countries and an insult in others.
senses.exampleCN: 进屋脱鞋在有些国家是文化规范，在另一些地方却可能被视为失礼。
senses.why: Politeness is the place where a culture's expectations become most visible, because the body itself is being directed.
senses.whyCN: 礼貌是文化期待最显眼的地方，因为被安排的是身体本身。

senses.title: A norm that varies across cultures
senses.definition: a standard whose content changes from one society to another, even when the situation is the same
senses.definitionCN: 同一情境下，内容随社会而变的标准
senses.example: Comparative studies list the cultural norm for greeting strangers in a dozen societies.
senses.exampleCN: 比较研究列出十几种社会里与陌生人打招呼的文化规范。
senses.why: The phrase is often used in the plural precisely to compare: each culture fills the same slot with different content.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语常用复数，正是为了比较：每种文化把同一个位置填进不同内容。

senses.title: An institutionalized cultural standard
senses.definition: a cultural expectation adopted by schools, courts or professions and enforced through formal rules
senses.definitionCN: 被学校、法院或行业采纳、并通过正式规则执行的文化期待
senses.example: The school uniform rule began as a cultural norm about neat dress.
senses.exampleCN: 校服规定最初是一条关于衣着整洁的文化规范。
senses.why: Institutions take a cultural expectation, write it down and attach consequences, turning custom into policy.
senses.whyCN: 机构把文化期待拿来写下、附上后果，习俗于是变成政策。

senses.title: A norm learned through enculturation
senses.titleCN: 通过文化濡化学得的规范
senses.definition: a norm absorbed while growing up inside a culture, often without explicit teaching
senses.definitionCN: 在一种文化中长大时吸收的规范，往往没有经过明教
senses.example: Children learn the cultural norm of greeting elders before they can explain why.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在能解释原因之前就学会了向长辈问好的文化规范。
senses.why: Enculturation is the process by which a culture installs its norms in a person, so the norm feels like second nature.
senses.whyCN: 文化濡化就是把规范装进一个人身上的过程，因此规范感觉像第二天性。

senses.title: A contested and negotiated norm
senses.definition: a norm whose content is disputed and renegotiated by different groups within the same culture
senses.definitionCN: 同一文化内部不同群体争夺并重新协商内容的规范
senses.example: The cultural norm about who pays on a date is still being argued over.
senses.exampleCN: 关于约会由谁付账的文化规范至今仍被争论。
senses.why: Cultures are not single voices, so any norm can become a site of struggle between generations or classes.
senses.whyCN: 文化不是单一声音，因此任何规范都可能成为代际或阶层争夺的场所。

senses.title: Abstract: any cultural standard
senses.definition: any standard by which a culture decides that behaviour is proper, admirable or shameful
senses.definitionCN: 一种文化用来判定行为得体、可敬或可耻的任何标准
senses.example: Every school of art challenges some cultural norm about beauty.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个艺术流派都会挑战某种关于美的文化规范。
senses.why: At its widest the phrase names the judging lens itself, whatever the culture happens to be looking at.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个短语命名的是那面评判的透镜本身，无论它在看什么。

intro.en: Cultural norm pairs cultura, Latin for tending and cultivation, with norma, a carpenter's square. The social sense of culture is modern, and the compound is a twentieth-century term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultural norm 把表示「耕作、培养」的拉丁 cultura 与表示「曲尺」的拉丁 norma 配在一起。culture 的社会义是近代产物，这个合成短语则是二十世纪的术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cultura meant 'tending, cultivation, care', from colere 'to till, inhabit, worship'. The farming image was extended to the care of the mind.
items.cn: cultura 意为「照料、耕作、培养」，来自 colere「耕种、居住、敬奉」。农耕意象后来扩展到对心智的照料。

items.en: Norma meant 'carpenter's square, rule, pattern'; its deeper origin is uncertain, and a link to Greek gnomon is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: norma 意为「木匠的曲尺、规则、范型」；更深来源不确定，与希腊 gnomon 的联系只是假说。

items.en: Culturalis, 'of cultivation', was formed from cultura plus an adjective ending; English cultural followed the same pattern much later.
items.cn: culturalis「耕作的、培养的」由 cultura 加形容词词尾构成；英语 cultural 很久以后才照同一模式出现。

items.en: English culture first meant the tilling of land. From the eighteenth century it widened to the whole way of life of a people, especially in German-influenced thought.
items.cn: 英语 culture 最初指耕地。从十八世纪起，它扩展为一个民族的全部生活方式，尤其在受德语影响的思想中。

items.en: Twentieth-century anthropology and sociology made cultural norm a standard term for the expectations a culture transmits to its members.
items.cn: 二十世纪的人类学与社会学把 cultural norm 变成标准术语，指一种文化传给其成员的期待。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first printed use of the exact compound is not recorded, the pre-Latin origin of colere is reconstructed, and norma remains etymologically unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个确切合成短语最早印行于何时没有记录；colere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式；norma 的词源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from the bare group rule and from a look-alike meaning 'refined'; group two holds words for handed-down practice.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与单纯的群体规则、以及意为「有教养的」形近词分开；第二组是表示世代沿袭做法的词。

entries.definition: A rule shared by any group, such as a queue or a classroom; a cultural norm adds the inheritance of a whole way of life.
entries.definitionCN: 任何群体共享的规则，如排队或课堂；文化规范则多了整套生活方式的传承。

entries.definition: A belief about what is good or important; a norm is an expectation about behaviour that follows from such beliefs.
entries.definitionCN: 关于何为善或重要的信念；规范则是由这类信念推出的行为期待。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who has acquired refinement; it describes a person, not a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一个人有修养的形容词；它描述人，不描述规则。

entries.definition: From Latin ager 'field' plus cultura; it keeps the farming sense that culture later left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ager「田地」加 cultura；它保留了 culture 后来丢掉的农耕义。

entries.definition: A traditional practice handed down over time; it describes what people do, while a norm also judges what they ought to do.
entries.definitionCN: 沿时间传下的传统做法；它描述人们做什么，而规范还评判人应当做什么。

entries.definition: The whole body of inherited practices and beliefs; a norm is one specific expectation inside that body.
entries.definitionCN: 继承下来的做法与信念的整体；规范只是这个整体里的一条具体期待。

entries.definition: The moral norms of a society, felt as sacred; cultural norms can be merely about manners.
entries.definitionCN: 一个社会被视为神圣的道德规范；文化规范也可以只关乎礼节。

entries.definition: An agreed way of doing something, often formal and recent; a cultural norm is usually older and deeper.
entries.definitionCN: 经约定形成的做法，往往正式且较新；文化规范通常更古老、更深。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Culture began as cultivation, so a cultural norm is a rule grown in a particular soil.
normal.cn: culture 最初是耕作，所以文化规范是在特定土壤里长出来的规则。

normal.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, so the second half of the phrase is a measuring tool.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，所以短语的后半段是一把量具。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the contrast: local cultural norms, cultural norm differences.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出对照：当地文化规范、文化规范差异。

normal.en: The plural is usual when cultures are compared, because each fills the same slot differently.
normal.cn: 比较文化时常用复数，因为每种文化把同一个位置填进不同内容。

normal.en: Culture also gives the verb cultivate, keeping the image of tending something until it grows.
normal.cn: culture 还衍生出动词 cultivate，保留「照料直到长成」的意象。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway where every visitor, without being told, leaves their shoes in the same spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门口，每位来客都不用谁提醒，就把鞋留在同一个位置。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe nobody writes down, yet every kitchen in the village cooks it the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一份没人写下的菜谱，村里每间厨房却都照同样方法做。

abstract.en: Picture a measuring square handed from parent to child, the marks worn smooth by use.
abstract.cn: 想象一把曲尺由父母交给孩子，刻度被使用磨得发亮。

examples.en: The cultural norm of bowing varies sharply between the two cities.
examples.cn: 鞠躬的文化规范在这两座城市之间差别很大。

examples.en: Migrant families often keep a cultural norm their neighbours have never seen.
examples.cn: 移民家庭常保留着邻居从未见过的文化规范。

examples.en: Fieldwork records how a cultural norm is taught to children without words.
examples.cn: 田野调查记录一条文化规范如何在没有言语的情况下教给孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考尔雀罗 诺姆」——一种文化在自家土壤里量行为的曲尺 → 文化规范

root: 拉丁 cultura「耕作、培养」+ 拉丁 norma「曲尺、规则」；cultura 来自 colere「耕种、照料」，norma 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the culture's shared expectation and spread to handed-down custom, politeness, cross-cultural variation, institutional rules, enculturation, dispute and finally any cultural standard.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从文化内部共享的期待出发，再扩展到传承习俗、礼貌、跨文化差异、制度规则、文化濡化、争议，最后是任何文化标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a culture grows its members like a garden, and a worn wooden square marks the line they should not cross.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种文化像照料园子一样养大成员，一把磨旧的木曲尺标出他们不该越过的线。

branches.en: GROWN AND INHERITED: an expectation held in common, then passed down until it becomes custom.
branches.cn: 培养与继承：先是共同持有的期待，再被传下去，直到成为习俗。

branches.en: BODY AND BORDER: politeness directs the body, and comparison shows each culture filling the slot differently.
branches.cn: 身体与边界：礼貌指挥身体，比较则显示每种文化把位置填进不同内容。

branches.en: WRITTEN BY INSTITUTIONS: schools and courts adopt the expectation and attach consequences.
branches.cn: 由机构写下：学校与法院采纳这条期待，并附上后果。

branches.en: ABSORBED IN CHILDHOOD: enculturation installs the norm before a child can explain it.
branches.cn: 童年吸收：文化濡化在孩子能解释之前就装进了规范。

branches.en: DISPUTED LENS: insiders argue over the content, and at its widest the phrase names the judging lens itself.
branches.cn: 可争的透镜：内部人为内容争论；推到最宽，短语命名的是评判透镜本身。

intro.en: A cultural norm joins two Latin nouns, one from the language of farming and one from the carpenter's bench.
intro.cn: cultural norm 把两个拉丁名词接在一起，一个来自农耕语汇，一个来自木匠的工作台。

latinIntro.en: Latin cultura gives culture, cultural, cultivate and cultivation; Latin norma gives norm, normal, normative and normalize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cultura 衍生 culture、cultural、cultivate 与 cultivation；拉丁 norma 衍生 norm、normal、normative 与 normalize。

items.example: The first half begins in the garden.
items.exampleCN: 前半段从园子开始。

items.example: Colere is the verb behind cultura.
items.exampleCN: colere 是 cultura 背后的动词。

items.example: Culture moved from fields to people.
items.exampleCN: culture 从田地移到人身上。

items.example: Cultural marks what belongs to a way of life.
items.exampleCN: cultural 标出属于某种生活方式的东西。

items.meaning: to tend so that something grows
items.example: Cultivate keeps the gardening image alive.
items.exampleCN: cultivate 让园艺意象继续活着。

items.example: The second half supplies the measure.
items.exampleCN: 后半段提供量具。

items.example: Norm makes the square abstract.
items.exampleCN: norm 把曲尺抽象化。

items.structure: norm plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'
items.example: Normative says what ought to be.
items.exampleCN: normative 说的是「应当如何」。

items.structure: cultural plus a suffix of manner
items.example: Culturally compares two ways of life.
items.exampleCN: culturally 用来比较两种生活方式。

definition_zh: 因循惯例；常规性；对既定习俗与形式的遵从
definition_en: the quality of following established customs, forms and expectations
core_image: 一排排相同的窗、相同的门牌、相同的窗帘长度，街道像照着同一张图纸长出来
scene: 老式婚礼上，长辈坚持按旧顺序敬茶、拍照、入席，年轻人只好照着走。The wedding followed the conventionality of an older generation, from tea to photographs to seating.
sceneCN: 这里 conventionality 指对既定习俗与程序的遵从（第 1 个义项：按惯例办事的性质）；句意为这场婚礼照着老一辈的惯例，从敬茶、拍照到入席一一照做。

pos.zh: 因循惯例；常规性（不可数，指性质或状态）
具体的惯例言行（用复数 conventionalities，指若干客套做法）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指若干具体惯例）

derivatives.zh: 惯例；会议（由拉丁 conventio「聚在一起、约定」经古法语进入英语，从聚会转指共同约定）
惯例的；因循的（由 convention 加表示「属于」的后缀构成，转指照既定形式办事）
按惯例地（由 conventional 加表示「方式」的后缀构成，转指以惯例为尺度）
不落俗套的（由表示否定的前缀加 conventional 构成，转指脱离既定形式）
召集；集会（由拉丁 convenire「聚到一起」直接借入，保留「走到一处」的动作义）
方便；便利（同出 convenire，由「相合、适配」转指省事合宜）

senses.title: Following accepted customs
senses.definition: the habit or quality of doing things in the way that has long been accepted
senses.definitionCN: 按长期被接受的方式办事的习惯或性质
senses.example: The wedding followed the conventionality of an older generation, from tea to photographs to seating.
senses.exampleCN: 这场婚礼照着老一辈的惯例，从敬茶、拍照到入席一一照做。
senses.why: The word names a quality rather than a single act: it is the tendency to let the accepted order decide the order of events.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一种性质，而非单个动作：让被接受的次序来决定事件次序的倾向。

senses.title: Being ordinary and unoriginal
senses.definition: the quality of being predictable, unoriginal or unadventurous
senses.definitionCN: 可预测、缺乏原创、不敢冒险的性质
senses.example: Critics complained about the conventionality of the plot, not its craft.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抱怨的是情节的陈旧，而不是技巧。
senses.why: A second judgement attaches to the same quality: following the accepted can look safe or merely dull.
senses.whyCN: 同一种性质还带着第二种评价：照既定路子走，可以显得稳妥，也可以显得乏味。

senses.title: Conventional phrasing or formality
senses.definition: the use of fixed polite phrases and forms rather than fresh or personal expression
senses.definitionCN: 使用固定的礼貌说法与形式，而非新鲜或个人的表达
senses.example: The letter opened with the conventionality of a formal greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信以正式问候的客套话开头。
senses.why: Language has ready-made forms for recurring situations, and their use is itself a kind of social compliance.
senses.whyCN: 语言为反复出现的情境准备了现成形式，使用这些形式本身就是一种社会遵从。

senses.title: Norm-driven social behaviour
senses.titleCN: 由规范驱动的社会行为
senses.definition: behaviour guided by what a group expects rather than by private preference
senses.definitionCN: 由群体期待而非个人偏好引导的行为
senses.example: The conventionality of the neighbourhood kept everyone's curtains the same length.
senses.exampleCN: 街区的因循惯例让每家的窗帘长度都一样。
senses.why: Here the abstract quality becomes visible in a street: shared expectations turn into repeated physical details.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象性质在街道上显形：共享期待变成重复的物理细节。

senses.title: Adherence to established forms in art
senses.definition: the reliance on established rules, genres or techniques instead of breaking them
senses.definitionCN: 依赖既定规则、体裁或技法，而非打破它们
senses.example: The composer's conventionality made the symphony easy to predict but hard to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作曲家的程式化让交响曲容易预测，却难以记住。
senses.why: Art criticism uses the word to measure how far a work stays inside the rules of its genre.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评用这个词衡量一件作品在多大程度上留在其体裁规则之内。

senses.title: Mere formality without substance
senses.definition: the state of keeping up a ceremony or courtesy after its meaning has gone
senses.definitionCN: 意义消失后仍维持仪式或礼节的状况
senses.example: The committee's conventionality produced minutes but no decision.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的例行程序产出了会议记录，却没有决定。
senses.why: When form outlives purpose, the same word turns from praise to complaint: it now means hollow compliance.
senses.whyCN: 当形式活得比目的更久，同一个词就从称赞变成抱怨：它现在指空洞的遵从。

senses.title: Compliance as social lubricant
senses.definition: the everyday compliance that lets strangers act together without negotiating every step
senses.definitionCN: 让陌生人不必逐步协商也能共同行动的日常遵从
senses.example: A little conventionality lets a crowded train load without argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一点因循惯例让拥挤的列车不吵不闹地装满人。
senses.why: The quality is not only a constraint; it is also the grease that saves everyone from explaining themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质不只是约束，也是省去人人自我解释的润滑剂。

senses.title: Abstract: predictability through shared rules
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：共享规则带来的可预期性
senses.definition: the predictability that arises when many people follow the same unwritten rules
senses.definitionCN: 许多人遵守同一套不成文规则时产生的可预期性
senses.example: Markets rely on the conventionality of strangers more than on written contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 市场依赖陌生人的惯例，胜过依赖书面合同。
senses.why: At its most abstract the word names the reliability that shared rules create, apart from any single rule.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个词命名的是共享规则造成的可靠性，与任何单条规则无关。

intro.en: Conventionality is convention plus two suffixes. Convention comes from Latin conventio, 'a meeting, an agreement', built on convenire 'to come together'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conventionality 是 convention 加两层后缀构成。convention 来自拉丁 conventio「聚会、约定」，其动词 convenire 意为「走到一起」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Venire meant 'to come'. It is the base of many English words about arriving, assembling or intervening.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」。它是许多表示到达、聚集或介入的英语词的基底。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus venire produced convenire 'to come together, assemble, agree'.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 venire 构成 convenire「走到一起、集会、达成一致」。

items.en: Conventio named a meeting or an agreement, and from 'what has been agreed' came the sense of an accepted practice.
items.cn: conventio 指聚会或约定，又从「已经商定之事」引申出「被接受的做法」。

items.en: Old French convention carried the word into English, where convention first meant an assembly and later a accepted custom.
items.cn: 古法语 convention 把这个词带进英语，convention 最初指集会，后来指被接受的习俗。

items.en: Conventional added an adjective ending to convention; conventionality then added a suffix of quality, naming the state of being conventional.
items.cn: conventional 由 convention 加形容词词尾构成；conventionality 再加表示性质的后缀，命名「因循」这一状态。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first printed use of conventionality is not recorded, though it is generally dated to the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：conventionality 最早印行于何时没有记录，一般认为在十七世纪。

note.en: Group one holds the same Latin 'come together' family plus one look-alike from a different root; group two holds words for social compliance.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「走到一起」词族的词，外加一个异源形近词；第二组是表示社会遵从的词。

entries.definition: The accepted practice or formal assembly; conventionality is the quality of following such practices.
entries.definitionCN: 被接受的做法或正式会议；conventionality 是遵从这类做法的性质。

entries.definition: Describing something that follows convention; the noun names the quality behind that description.
entries.definitionCN: 形容照惯例行事的事物；名词则命名这一形容背后的性质。

entries.definition: Also from convenire, but it means ease or suitability, not adherence to custom.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 convenire，却指方便或合宜，而非对习俗的遵从。

entries.definition: From Latin vincere 'to conquer', not venire. It means a firm belief or a court finding, with no custom sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vincere「征服」，并非 venire；它指坚定信念或法庭判定，没有习俗义。

entries.definition: Behaviour that matches the group; it stresses what people do, while conventionality stresses the established forms they follow.
entries.definitionCN: 与群体一致的行为；它强调人做什么，而 conventionality 强调人所遵循的既定形式。

entries.definition: Strict adherence to an approved doctrine, usually religious or political; it is stronger and more doctrinal.
entries.definitionCN: 对获准教义的严格遵守，通常指宗教或政治；语气更强，也更教条。

entries.definition: The quality of being formal or ceremonial; it can exist without the wider social custom that conventionality names.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或合乎礼仪的性质；它可以不带 conventionality 所指的更广社会习俗。

entries.definition: A handed-down way of doing something; conventionality is the disposition to keep to such ways.
entries.definitionCN: 世代沿袭的做法；conventionality 是守着这类做法的倾向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Convenir means come together, so a convention is first a gathering, then what the gathering agrees on.
normal.cn: convenire 意为走到一起，所以 convention 先是聚会，再是聚会商定之事。

normal.en: Conventionality adds a suffix of quality, turning the practice into a disposition.
normal.cn: conventionality 加一层表示性质的后缀，把做法变成倾向。

normal.en: Fixed phrases test the tone: strict conventionality, mere conventionality, break with conventionality.
normal.cn: 固定说法试出语气：严格因循、仅仅是客套、打破惯例。

normal.en: Convenience shares the same root but means ease, not compliance, so the two must not be swapped.
normal.cn: convenience 同根却指方便，不指遵从，二者不可互换。

normal.en: The adjective is conventional and the adverb conventionally; the noun keeps the abstract quality.
normal.cn: 形容词是 conventional，副词是 conventionally，名词保留抽象性质。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every curtain stops at the same height, though no rule says so.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，家家窗帘都停在同样的高度，却没有任何规则这样要求。

abstract.en: Picture a wedding rehearsal where every step has a fixed order and a fixed phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象一场婚礼排练，每一步都有固定次序与固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that runs smoothly only because every part repeats the same motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器之所以顺畅，只因为每个部件重复同一个动作。

examples.en: The architect's conventionality made the building easy to approve and hard to love.
examples.cn: 这位建筑师的因循让方案容易获批，却难以让人喜爱。

examples.en: A little conventionality keeps a shared office peaceful.
examples.cn: 一点因循惯例能让共享办公室保持平静。

examples.en: The novel mocks the conventionality of its own ending.
examples.cn: 这部小说嘲讽自己结局的程式化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康文 申 那里提」——大家走到一起商定下来的老规矩 → 因循惯例

root: 拉丁 convenire「走到一起、达成一致」+ 拉丁 conventio「聚会、约定」；后加表示性质的拉丁后缀构成，一般认为十七世纪出现于英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat the quality as a disposition to keep to accepted forms, then show it as dullness, fixed phrasing, street-level repetition, artistic rule-keeping, hollow ceremony, social lubrication and finally predictability itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把这个性质看作守着既定形式的倾向，再依次显示为陈旧、程式化说法、街道层面的重复、艺术上的守规、空洞仪式、社交润滑，最后是可预期性本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street built from one drawing, every window and curtain repeating the same measurement.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条照着同一张图纸建成的街，每扇窗、每幅窗帘都重复同一个尺寸。

branches.en: THE DISPOSITION AND ITS STREET: a habit of following accepted order, visible in repeated physical details.
branches.cn: 倾向与它的街道：遵从既定次序的习惯，显形为重复的物理细节。

branches.en: SAFE OR DULL: the same quality read as unoriginality, and as reliance on established artistic forms.
branches.cn: 稳妥或乏味：同一性质既被读作陈旧，也被读作依赖既定艺术形式。

branches.en: FORM WITHOUT SPIRIT: fixed polite phrasing, then ceremony kept up after its meaning has gone.
branches.cn: 有形式无精神：先是固定客套话，再是意义消失后仍维持的仪式。

branches.en: SOCIAL LUBRICANT: compliance saves strangers from negotiating every step.
branches.cn: 社交润滑：遵从让陌生人省去逐步协商。

branches.en: PREDICTABILITY: the widest reading names the reliability shared rules create.
branches.cn: 可预期性：最宽的读法命名共享规则造成的可靠性。

intro.en: Conventionality is a Latin verb, a noun of agreement and two English suffixes stacked on one stem.
intro.cn: conventionality 是一个拉丁动词、一个表示约定的名词，再在同一个词干上叠两层英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire gives convene, convention, convenient, intervene and prevent; the same stem builds conventionality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 venire 衍生 convene、convention、convenient、intervene 与 prevent；同一词干还构成 conventionality。

items.example: The root is the act of coming.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是「来」的动作。

items.example: Convenire is the gathering before the agreement.
items.exampleCN: convenire 是先于约定的聚集。

items.structure: convenire plus a noun of action
items.example: Conventio turns the gathering into a settled thing.
items.exampleCN: conventio 把聚集变成已定之事。

items.example: Convention moved from meeting to custom.
items.exampleCN: convention 从集会转向习俗。

items.example: Conventional describes the practice.
items.exampleCN: conventional 描述这种做法。

items.structure: conventional plus a suffix of quality
items.example: The noun names the disposition itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名倾向本身。

items.example: The negative shows how strong the expectation is.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式显示这种期待有多强。

items.structure: convenire plus a suffix of fitness
items.example: Convenience keeps the 'fit together' side of the root.
items.exampleCN: convenience 保留词根里「相合」的一面。

items.example: Convene is the plain verb of gathering.
items.exampleCN: convene 是表示聚集的普通动词。

definition_zh: 集体的；共同的；集体（一群人作为一个整体）
definition_en: shared by or involving a group of people acting as one body
core_image: 许多人把各自的一小捆麦子并到同一块晒场上，单看每人都不多，合起来却堆成一座金色的小山
scene: 收获季节，几家农户把自家的果子倒进同一辆卡车，按出力多少分红。The farmers sold the harvest through a collective that shared both the truck and the profit.
sceneCN: 这里 collective 指由成员共同拥有并共同管理的组织（第 2 个义项：作为一个整体行动的人群）；句意为农户们通过一个共同拥有卡车与收益的集体把收成卖出去。

pos.zh: 集体的；共同的；由一群人共同做出的
集体；共同组织（如合作社、集体农庄）

derivatives.zh: 收集；聚集（由拉丁 colligere「聚到一起」经法语进入英语，保留「把散的东西归拢」的动作义）
收藏；收集（由 collect 加表示「动作结果」的后缀构成，转指归拢起来的一批东西）
集体主义（由 collective 加表示「主义」的后缀构成，转指主张群体优先的制度或信念）
集体主义者；集体主义的（由 collectivism 加表示「人」的后缀构成）
使集体化（由 collective 加表示「使成为」的后缀构成，转指把私有转为集体所有）
集体性；整体（由 collective 加表示「性质」的后缀构成，转指作为整体的状态）

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: held or experienced by many people together rather than by one person alone
senses.definitionCN: 由许多人共同持有或经历，而非一个人独自持有
senses.example: The village made a collective decision to rebuild the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 全村共同决定重修这座桥。
senses.why: The adjective takes a singular act and spreads its subject across many people, so the actor is the group.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把单个动作的主语铺到许多人身上，行动者于是成了群体。

senses.title: A group acting as one body
senses.definition: an organized group that owns or decides something as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 作为单一单位拥有或决定某事的组织化群体
senses.example: The farmers sold the harvest through a collective that shared both the truck and the profit.
senses.exampleCN: 农户们通过一个共同拥有卡车与收益的集体把收成卖出去。
senses.why: The noun turns the adjective into an entity: what is shared becomes an organization that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 名词把形容词变成实体：被共享的东西变成持有它的组织。

senses.title: A collective farm or enterprise
senses.definition: a farm or business owned and run jointly by its workers rather than by private owners
senses.definitionCN: 由劳动者共同拥有和经营、而非私人业主所有的农场或企业
senses.example: Her grandparents worked on a collective outside the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母在城外一个集体农庄劳动。
senses.why: Modern history gave the noun a concrete institutional form, especially in socialist economies.
senses.whyCN: 现代历史给这个名词一个具体的制度形态，尤其在社会主义经济中。

senses.title: A collective noun in grammar
senses.definition: a singular noun that names a group, such as team or family, and may take a singular or plural verb
senses.definitionCN: 命名一个群体的单数名词，如 team 或 family，可搭配单数或复数动词
senses.example: The grammar book lists committee among the collective nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 这本语法书把 committee 列为集合名词。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the adjective because one word stands for many members, exactly the pattern the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个形容词，因为一个词代表许多成员，正是这个词所描述的格局。

senses.title: The collective unconscious
senses.definition: a shared layer of inherited images and patterns that a psychologist treats as common to a whole people
senses.definitionCN: 一层共享的、继承下来的意象与模式，被心理学家视为整个民族共有
senses.example: Jung argued that myths draw on the collective unconscious.
senses.exampleCN: 荣格主张神话取材于集体无意识。
senses.why: Psychology extended the adjective inward, making the shared thing a layer of the mind rather than an organization.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这个形容词向内延伸，使共享之物成为心智的一层，而不是一个组织。

senses.title: Collective action or bargaining
senses.definition: organized joint action by many people to pursue a shared interest, especially at work
senses.definitionCN: 许多人为共同利益组织的联合行动，尤指劳动场合
senses.example: Collective bargaining set the wage for the whole factory.
senses.exampleCN: 集体谈判为全厂定下工资。
senses.why: Labour law uses the word for the moment when separate workers act as one negotiating party.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法用这个词指分散的工人作为一个谈判方行动的时刻。

senses.title: Collective memory or identity
senses.definition: the shared recollection or self-image through which a group understands who it is
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体借以理解自身是谁的共享记忆或自我形象
senses.example: The old harbour survives in the city's collective memory.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港留在城市的集体记忆里。
senses.why: The adjective moves from ownership to meaning: what a group shares can be a past and a sense of itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从所有权移到意义：群体共享的可以是过去与自我认识。

senses.title: Abstract: an emergent whole
senses.definition: a whole formed by many parts whose joint behaviour cannot be reduced to any one part
senses.definitionCN: 由许多部分构成、其联合行为不能还原为任何单个部分的整体
senses.example: A flock's collective motion appears even though no bird carries the pattern alone.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟群的集体运动出现了，尽管没有一只鸟独自携带这个格局。
senses.why: At its most abstract the word names a whole that exists only because the parts act together.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个词命名一个只因各部分共同行动才存在的整体。

intro.en: Collective comes from Latin collectivus, built on colligere 'to gather together', from com- 'together' plus legere 'to gather, choose'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collective 来自拉丁 collectivus，其基底 colligere 意为「聚到一起」，由表示「一起」的成分加 legere「收集、挑选」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Legere meant 'to gather, pick out, read'. The gathering sense is the one behind collect, while the reading sense gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑出、阅读」。collect 取的是「收集」义，而「阅读」义衍生 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus legere produced colligere 'to gather together, assemble'.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 legere 构成 colligere「聚到一起、集合」。

items.en: Collectivus meant 'of gathering' or 'gathered'; the adjective later named what belongs to a group as a whole.
items.cn: collectivus 意为「收集的、被收集的」；这个形容词后来指属于整个群体的东西。

items.en: French collectif and English collective carried the adjective into social and political writing in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 法语 collectif 与英语 collective 在十六、十七世纪把这个形容词带进社会与政治写作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the noun acquired its institutional sense, especially for jointly owned farms and enterprises.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个名词获得制度义，尤指共同拥有的农场与企业。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Indo-European root behind legere is a reconstruction, and the first use of the noun for a cooperative body is not precisely recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：legere 背后的印欧词根属重构形式；这个名词最早何时指合作社团，没有精确记录。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from words of the same gathering root; group two holds near synonyms for what is shared.
note.cn: 第一组把形容词与同出「收集」词根的词分开；第二组是表示「共同」的近义词。

entries.definition: To gather things or people; the adjective describes what a gathered group shares.
entries.definitionCN: 收集物或人；形容词描述聚起来的群体所共享的东西。

entries.definition: A group of gathered objects or the act of gathering; it has no social-body sense.
entries.definitionCN: 收集起来的一批东西或收集动作；没有社会群体的意思。

entries.definition: From Latin collegium 'a body of colleagues', built on legare 'to send as a deputy', not legere.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 collegium「同僚团体」，基底是 legare「派为使节」，并非 legere。

entries.definition: From Latin collega 'one sent together with another', also from legare, so it is not a relative of collective.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 collega「被一同派出的人」，同样出自 legare，因此不是 collective 的同族词。

entries.definition: Shared by a community, often in the sense of common ownership or common use; collective is broader and can be organisational.
entries.definitionCN: 由共同体共享，常指共有或共用；collective 更宽，也可指组织化的。

entries.definition: Held in common by two or more people; it is the everyday word that collective formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个或更多人共同持有；这是 collective 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: Done or held by two or more parties together, often of an action or account; it stresses the parties rather than the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同做出或持有，常指行动或账户；它强调各方，而非整体。

entries.definition: Of a corporation or an organized body; it stresses legal structure, while collective stresses shared membership.
entries.definitionCN: 属于公司或有组织的团体；它强调法律结构，collective 强调共享成员身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Legere means gather, so a collective is what has been gathered into one body.
normal.cn: legere 意为收集，所以 collective 就是被收拢成一个整体的东西。

normal.en: Com- means together, so the word already carries the coming-together of many parts.
normal.cn: 表示「一起」的成分说明这个词本身就带着多部分聚合。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: collective action, collective memory, collective ownership.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示范围：集体行动、集体记忆、集体所有。

normal.en: The noun is often an organization: a farm, a cooperative, a body of workers.
normal.cn: 名词常指组织：农庄、合作社、工人团体。

normal.en: The adverb collectively marks the group as a single actor.
normal.cn: 副词 collectively 把群体标为单一行动者。

abstract.en: Picture many small bundles of wheat laid on one threshing floor until they become one heap.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小捆麦子铺到同一块打谷场上，最后堆成一座山。

abstract.en: Picture a flock turning together although no single bird knows the turn.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟群一起转向，尽管没有一只鸟知道这个转向。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with one account shared by a whole village.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，整个村子共用同一个账户。

examples.en: The workers bought the mill as a collective and ran it themselves.
examples.cn: 工人们以集体名义买下磨坊，自己经营。

examples.en: Collective memory of the flood shaped where the new houses were built.
examples.cn: 关于那场洪水的集体记忆决定了新房子建在哪里。

examples.en: Collective action succeeded because every shop closed on the same day.
examples.cn: 集体行动成功，因为所有店铺在同一天关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可来客体舞」——把大家收拢到一起，合成一个身体 → 集体的

root: 拉丁 colligere「聚到一起」= 表示「一起」的成分 + legere「收集、挑选」；其印欧词根 *leg- 为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a group sharing one act, then turn the group into an entity, a farm, a grammatical class, a mental layer, a negotiating party, a shared past and finally an emergent whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先讲群体共同承担一个动作，再把群体变成实体、农庄、语法类别、心智层次、谈判方、共享过去，最后是涌现出的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small bundles laid on one floor become a single heap no bundle could make alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：小捆的东西铺到同一块场地上，合成一座任何单捆都堆不出的山。

branches.en: SHARED ACT AND SHARED WORD: many people act as one, and grammar lets one word stand for many.
branches.cn: 共享动作与共享词：许多人像一个那样行动，语法让一个词代表许多人。

branches.en: THE ENTITY: the shared thing becomes an organization, then a farm or enterprise with a legal form.
branches.cn: 实体：共享之物变成组织，再变成有法律形式的农庄或企业。

branches.en: INWARD AND BACKWARD: a shared mental layer, then a shared past and self-image.
branches.cn: 向内与向后：先是共享的心智层，再是共享的过去与自我形象。

branches.en: AS ONE PARTY: workers act jointly at the bargaining table.
branches.cn: 作为一方：工人在谈判桌上联合行动。

branches.en: EMERGENCE: a whole exists only because the parts move together.
branches.cn: 涌现：整体只因各部分共同运动而存在。

intro.en: Collective is a Latin adjective built from a verb of gathering and a prefix meaning 'together'.
intro.cn: collective 是一个拉丁形容词，由表示「收集」的动词与表示「一起」的前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere gives collect, select, elect, lecture and legend; com- adds the sense of gathering into one place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legere 衍生 collect、select、elect、lecture 与 legend；表示「一起」的前缀增添「收进一处」的意思。

items.example: The root supplies the gathering.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「收集」这一层。

items.example: Colligere is the gathering into one body.
items.exampleCN: colligere 是收拢成一个整体。

items.example: Collectivus turned the act into a quality.
items.exampleCN: collectivus 把动作变成性质。

items.example: Collect is the plain verb.
items.exampleCN: collect 是普通动词。

items.structure: collect plus a suffix of action or result
items.meaning: a gathering or the gathered set
items.example: Collection names the result.
items.exampleCN: collection 命名结果。

items.example: Collective applies the quality to a group.
items.exampleCN: collective 把这种性质用于群体。

items.structure: collective plus a suffix of doctrine
items.example: Collectivism turns the adjective into a political doctrine.
items.exampleCN: collectivism 把形容词变成政治主张。

items.example: Collectivize is the act of making collective.
items.exampleCN: collectivize 是使某物集体化的动作。

items.structure: collective plus a suffix of manner
items.example: Collectively marks the group as the actor.
items.exampleCN: collectively 把群体标为行动者。

definition_zh: 合作；协作；两个以上的人或团体共同从事一项工作；（历史）与占领者合作
definition_en: the act of working jointly with others on a shared task or project
core_image: 两个人各执绳子的一端，中间悬着一块沉重的石板，只有同时用力才能把它抬进门
scene: 两个实验室把各自的样本和数据放在同一张桌上，轮流守夜跑完整个实验。The collaboration between the two labs produced a result neither could have reached alone.
sceneCN: 这里 collaboration 指两个以上主体共同投入、完成一项工作的合作（第 1 个义项：共同劳动）；句意为两个实验室的合作产生了任何一方单独都无法达到的结果。

pos.zh: 合作；协作（不可数，指合作状态或活动）
一项具体的合作项目（可数，用复数 collaborations）

derivatives.zh: 合作；协作（由拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」经法语进入英语，保留「共同出力」的动作义）
协作的；合作的（由 collaborate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指以共同参与为特征）
合作者；协作者（由 collaborate 加表示「人」的后缀构成，转指共同出力的人）
实验室（同出拉丁 laborare「劳动」，由「劳作之处」转指进行实验的场所）
详述；精心制作的（由表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 laborare 构成，从「费力做出」转指细致加工）
费力的；艰苦的（由拉丁 labor「劳动」加表示「充满」的后缀构成，转指劳动量很大）

senses.title: Working together on a shared task
senses.definition: the act of two or more people or groups working jointly on the same task
senses.definitionCN: 两个以上的人或团体共同投入同一项工作的行为
senses.example: The collaboration between the two labs produced a result neither could have reached alone.
senses.exampleCN: 两个实验室的合作产生了任何一方单独都无法达到的结果。
senses.why: Collaboration is labour shared: the Latin verb joins 'together' to 'work', so the core is joint effort rather than mere contact.
senses.whyCN: collaboration 是共享的劳动：拉丁动词把「一起」接到「劳动」上，核心是共同出力，而非仅仅接触。

senses.title: Joint authorship or creation
senses.definition: the state of producing a book, work of art or invention together, with shared credit
senses.definitionCN: 共同完成书籍、艺术品或发明，并共享署名
senses.example: The album is a collaboration between a composer and a field recordist.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是一位作曲家与一位野外录音师的共同创作。
senses.why: When the joint work leaves a named product, the word shifts from the activity to the shared credit.
senses.whyCN: 当共同劳动留下具名成品，词义就从活动转到共享的署名。

senses.title: Wartime cooperation with an occupier
senses.definition: the act of working with an enemy occupier, treated as betrayal by compatriots
senses.definitionCN: 与敌方占领者合作，被同胞视为背叛的行为
senses.example: The post-war trials punished wartime collaboration with the occupying army.
senses.exampleCN: 战后审判惩罚了战时与占领军合作的行为。
senses.why: History gave the neutral word a dark sense: working together becomes treason when the partner is an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 历史给这个中性词添了黑暗义：当伙伴是敌人时，共同工作就变成叛国。

senses.title: Cross-disciplinary collaboration
senses.definition: joint work between specialists from different fields, each contributing a distinct method
senses.definitionCN: 不同领域的专家共同工作，各自贡献不同方法
senses.example: The climate report required collaboration between physicists and historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这份气候报告需要物理学家与历史学家协作。
senses.why: Complex problems no longer fit one department, so the word names the bridge between different expert languages.
senses.whyCN: 复杂问题不再属于单一部门，因此这个词命名不同专家语言之间的桥。

senses.title: Digital collaboration tools
senses.definition: the use of shared software and networks so that people can work on one file or project at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 使用共享软件与网络，使人们能远程处理同一文件或项目
senses.example: Remote collaboration improved once the team shared one editing space.
senses.exampleCN: 团队共用同一个编辑空间后，远程协作改善了。
senses.why: Technology extends the same joint labour across distance, turning a room into a network.
senses.whyCN: 技术把同一种共同劳动拉过距离，把一间屋子变成一张网络。

senses.title: A business partnership
senses.definition: a working arrangement between firms or departments for a shared commercial goal
senses.definitionCN: 企业或部门为共同商业目标形成的合作安排
senses.example: The two firms announced a collaboration to build the charging network.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司宣布合作建设充电网络。
senses.why: Commerce uses the word for a bounded arrangement: the parties remain separate but pool part of their work.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词指有边界的安排：各方仍独立，但把部分工作合在一起。

senses.title: Scientific collaboration
senses.definition: joint research by scientists who share data, instruments or authorship across institutions
senses.definitionCN: 科学家跨机构共享数据、仪器或署名权的研究合作
senses.example: The discovery rested on a long collaboration across three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发现依赖横跨三大洲的长期合作。
senses.why: Big science is rarely solitary, so the word becomes the normal label for shared instruments and shared papers.
senses.whyCN: 大科学很少单干，因此这个词成为共享仪器与共享论文的常规标签。

senses.title: Abstract: effort greater than its parts
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：合力超过部分之和
senses.definition: joint effort whose result exceeds what the participants could produce separately
senses.definitionCN: 其结果超过参与者各自单独所能产出的共同出力
senses.example: The essay argues that collaboration is not addition but a third mind.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章主张合作不是相加，而是生出第三个头脑。
senses.why: At its most abstract the word names the surplus that appears when separate skills interlock.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个词命名不同技能咬合时出现的盈余。

intro.en: Collaboration comes from Latin collaborare 'to work together', from com- 'together' plus laborare 'to work'. It entered English in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collaboration 来自拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」，由表示「一起」的成分加 laborare「劳动」构成。它在十九世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor meant 'work, toil, effort', and also 'a task'. It is the noun behind laborious and laboratory.
items.cn: labor 意为「劳动、辛苦、努力」，也指「一项任务」。它是 laborious 与 laboratory 背后的名词。

items.en: Laborare meant 'to work, toil, take pains'. The verb keeps the physical effort of the noun.
items.cn: laborare 意为「劳动、辛苦、费心」。这个动词保留了名词里的体力付出。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare produced collaborare 'to work together'. The Latin verb had no political colour.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 laborare 构成 collaborare「一起劳动」。这个拉丁动词没有政治色彩。

items.en: French collaboration and English collaboration appeared in the nineteenth century for joint work in science, letters and business.
items.cn: 法语 collaboration 与英语 collaboration 在十九世纪出现，指科学、文学与商业中的共同工作。

items.en: During the Second World War the same word was applied to cooperation with an occupying power, and this negative sense became fixed in many languages.
items.cn: 第二次世界大战期间，同一个词被用于指与占领国合作，这一负面义在多种语言中固定下来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first printed English use of collaboration is not precisely recorded, and the exact date when the wartime sense became standard is disputed.
