items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：collaboration 在英语中最早印行于何时没有精确记录；战时义何时成为标准说法也有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the word from other Latin verbs of working together; group two holds the everyday names for joint work.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与其他表示共同工作的拉丁动词分开；第二组是共同劳动的日常说法。

entries.definition: From Latin cooperari, built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. It stresses mutual help more than a shared project.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cooperari，基底是 operari「工作」与 opus「工作」。它更强调互相帮助，而非共同项目。

entries.definition: From Latin ordinare 'to arrange in order'. It means keeping activities in step, not doing the work together.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ordinare「按次序安排」。它指让活动步调一致，而非一起做同一件事。

entries.definition: From Latin colludere 'to play together', built on ludere 'to play'. It means a secret, often dishonest agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 colludere「一起玩」，基底是 ludere「玩」。它指秘密且常不正当的串通。

entries.definition: From Latin collega, built on legare 'to send as a deputy', not laborare. A colleague is a fellow worker, not the joint work.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 collega，基底是 legare「派为使节」，并非 laborare。同事是一起工作的人，不是共同工作本身。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for people working well together; collaboration is its formal and project-oriented counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们配合良好的日常名词；collaboration 是其正式、以项目为导向的对应词。

entries.definition: A formal arrangement between parties, often legal and long-term; collaboration can be a single project.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式安排，常带法律与长期性质；collaboration 可以只是一个项目。

entries.definition: Willing help offered to another's effort; it does not require a shared product or shared credit.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意协助他人的努力；它不要求共同成品或共同署名。

entries.definition: A formal union of parties for a common aim, usually political or military; it stresses the bond rather than the work.
entries.definitionCN: 各方为共同目标结成的正式联盟，通常指政治或军事；它强调纽带而非劳动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Laborare means to work, so collaboration is literally working together.
normal.cn: laborare 意为劳动，所以 collaboration 字面上就是一起劳动。

normal.en: The 'together' prefix is the same one in collect and cooperate, but only this verb attaches it to work.
normal.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀与 collect、cooperate 相同，但只有这个动词把它接到「劳动」上。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: research collaboration, international collaboration, in collaboration with.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出尺度：研究合作、国际合作、与……合作。

normal.en: Laboratory shares the work root: a place of work became a place of experiment.
normal.cn: laboratory 共享「劳动」词根：劳作之处变成了实验之处。

normal.en: The wartime sense is the dark twin: the same joint work, now with an enemy.
normal.cn: 战时义是它的黑暗双生：同一种共同劳动，伙伴换成了敌人。

abstract.en: Picture two people holding opposite ends of one rope around a heavy stone.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人各执一根绳子的两端，绕着一块沉重的石头。

abstract.en: Picture two hands correcting the same drawing, each line continuing the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在同一张图上改线，每条线都接着另一条。

abstract.en: Picture a third mind appearing between two speakers as they talk.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人说话时，在他们之间出现第三个头脑。

examples.en: The bridge was built through collaboration between engineers and local masons.
examples.cn: 这座桥由工程师与本地石匠合作建成。

examples.en: International collaboration shortened the vaccine trial by years.
examples.cn: 国际合作把疫苗试验缩短了数年。

examples.en: The wartime collaboration still divides the town's memory.
examples.cn: 战时的通敌合作至今仍分裂着这座镇的记忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可 拉伯 雷 申」——一起出力把重东西抬起来 → 合作

root: 拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」= 表示「一起」的成分 + laborare「劳动」；后者来自 labor「劳动」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with shared labour, then move to shared credit, wartime betrayal, cross-disciplinary work, remote tools, business deals, big science and finally the surplus that appears when skills interlock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从共同劳动出发，转到共享署名、战时背叛、跨学科工作、远程工具、商业协议、大科学，最后是技能咬合时出现的盈余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on one rope, a heavy stone between them, neither able to lift it alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手握同一根绳，中间是一块沉重的石头，谁都单独抬不起来。

branches.en: WORK AND CREDIT: joint labour, then the shared name on what it produces.
branches.cn: 劳动与署名：先是共同出力，再是成品上的共同名字。

branches.en: THE DARK TWIN: the same joint work performed with an enemy occupier.
branches.cn: 黑暗双生：同一种共同劳动，伙伴换成敌方占领者。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: different disciplines and different institutions pool methods and instruments.
branches.cn: 跨越边界：不同学科与不同机构共享方法与仪器。

branches.en: TOOLS AND CONTRACTS: software carries the work across distance, and firms bound it with an agreement.
branches.cn: 工具与合同：软件把劳动拉过距离，公司用协议给它划界。

branches.en: SURPLUS: the result exceeds what any participant could make alone.
branches.cn: 盈余：结果超过任何参与者单独所能做出。

intro.en: Collaboration is a Latin verb of work with a prefix meaning 'together', plus a noun ending.
intro.cn: collaboration 是一个表示劳动的拉丁动词，带表示「一起」的前缀，再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor gives laborious and laboratory; laborare gives collaborate, collaboration and collaborator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 labor 衍生 laborious 与 laboratory；laborare 衍生 collaborate、collaboration 与 collaborator。

items.example: The root supplies the toil.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「辛苦」这一层。

items.example: Laborare is the act of working.
items.exampleCN: laborare 是劳动的动作。

items.example: Collaborare joins the prefix to the work.
items.exampleCN: collaborare 把前缀接到劳动上。

items.example: Collaborate is the English verb.
items.exampleCN: collaborate 是英语动词。

items.structure: collaborate plus a suffix of action
items.example: The noun names the joint activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名共同活动。

items.structure: collaborate plus a suffix meaning 'tending to'
items.example: Collaborative describes the arrangement.
items.exampleCN: collaborative 描述这种安排。

items.example: The person who shares the labour.
items.exampleCN: 共同出力的人。

items.structure: laborare plus a suffix of place
items.example: The work place became a research place.
items.exampleCN: 劳作之处变成研究之处。

items.example: To elaborate is to work something out fully.
items.exampleCN: elaborate 就是把某物完全做出来。

definition_zh: 协作的；合作的；以多方共同参与、共享贡献为特征的
definition_en: involving two or more people or groups working together on a shared task
core_image: 一张长桌上摊开同一份图纸，几只不同的手同时在同一处改线，笔迹彼此接着
scene: 老师在课堂上把学生分成小组，每组只拿到一部分线索，必须互相交换才能拼出答案。The teacher designed a collaborative task in which each group held only part of the clues.
sceneCN: 这里 collaborative 指以多方共同参与、共享贡献为特征的（第 1 个义项：协作式的）；句意为老师设计了一项协作任务，每组只掌握一部分线索。

pos.zh: 协作的；合作的；以共同参与为特征的
（工作方式）需要多方共享信息与贡献的

derivatives.zh: 合作；协作（由拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」经法语进入英语，保留共同出力的动作义）
合作；协作（由 collaborate 加表示「动作」的后缀构成，转指共同工作的活动或项目）
合作者；协作者（由 collaborate 加表示「人」的后缀构成，转指共同出力的人）
合作的；配合的（由拉丁 cooperari「共同工作」构成，与 collaborative 词根不同）
实验室（同出拉丁 laborare「劳动」，由「劳作之处」转指实验场所）
同僚的；同事式的（由拉丁 collegium「同僚团体」构成，词根与 collaborative 不同）

senses.title: Involving several parties
senses.definition: involving two or more people or groups who contribute to one shared task
senses.definitionCN: 涉及两个以上的人或团体共同为一项任务出力
senses.example: The teacher designed a collaborative task in which each group held only part of the clues.
senses.exampleCN: 老师设计了一项协作任务，每组只掌握一部分线索。
senses.why: The adjective marks the structure of an activity: no single party holds the whole task.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出活动的结构：没有任何一方掌握整个任务。

senses.title: Collaborative research
senses.definition: research in which several investigators share data, methods or authorship
senses.definitionCN: 多位研究者共享数据、方法或署名权的研究
senses.example: The paper was the product of a collaborative research programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文是一个协作研究项目的产物。
senses.why: Research became too large for one hand, so the adjective names work that is planned around shared input.
senses.whyCN: 研究规模超出单人所能承担，因此这个形容词命名围绕共享投入来规划的工作。

senses.title: Collaborative learning
senses.definition: classroom work in which students help each other understand rather than compete for grades
senses.definitionCN: 学生互相帮助理解、而非争夺分数的课堂工作
senses.example: Collaborative learning gave the quieter students a role in every group.
senses.exampleCN: 协作学习让较安静的学生在每个小组里都有角色。
senses.why: Education borrowed the word to describe a pedagogy in which knowledge is built between learners, not delivered to them.
senses.whyCN: 教育学借用这个词，描述一种知识在学习者之间共建、而非被单向送达的教学法。

senses.title: Collaborative software
senses.definition: software that lets several users edit, comment or decide in the same shared space
senses.definitionCN: 让多位用户在同一共享空间编辑、评论或决定的软件
senses.example: The team moved its minutes into a collaborative document.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把会议记录搬进了一份协作文档。
senses.why: The digital sense narrows the word to a tool: what is shared is the file, and the work happens at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 数字义把这个词收窄到工具：共享的是文件，劳动发生在远处。

senses.title: A collaborative decision process
senses.definition: a decision made through structured discussion among affected parties rather than by one authority
senses.definitionCN: 由受影响各方经过有结构的讨论、而非单一权威做出的决定
senses.example: The council adopted a collaborative process for choosing the site.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会采用协商式流程来选择地址。
senses.why: Governance uses the adjective for legitimacy: those who must live with a decision help make it.
senses.whyCN: 治理使用这个形容词来获得正当性：要与决定共处的人参与作出决定。

senses.title: The collaborative economy
senses.definition: an economy in which people share goods, services or platforms instead of only buying from firms
senses.definitionCN: 人们共享物品、服务或平台、而非只向公司购买的经济形态
senses.example: Bike sharing is an early example of the collaborative economy.
senses.exampleCN: 共享单车是协同经济的早期例子。
senses.why: The term widened joint use from a project to a whole market, where the platform is the shared thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语把共同使用从一个项目扩到整个市场，共享之物成了平台。

senses.title: A collaborative spirit
senses.definition: a willingness to share credit, listen and adjust one's own contribution
senses.definitionCN: 愿意共享功劳、倾听并调整自己贡献的态度
senses.example: Her collaborative spirit kept the two departments talking.
senses.exampleCN: 她乐于合作的态度让两个部门一直保持沟通。
senses.why: The adjective can describe a disposition, not only a structure: it names the temper that makes joint work possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也能描述气质，而不只是结构：它命名使共同工作成为可能的心性。

senses.title: Abstract: designed for shared contribution
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：为共同贡献而设计
senses.definition: designed so that the result depends on contributions from more than one source
senses.definitionCN: 其设计使结果依赖一个以上来源的贡献
senses.example: A good collaborative system makes every contribution visible.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好的协作系统让每一份贡献都可见。
senses.why: At its widest the adjective describes any arrangement whose design assumes many hands, whether or not they are present.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个形容词描述任何在设计上假定有许多只手的安排，无论那些手是否在场。

intro.en: Collaborative is collaborate plus the Latin adjective ending -ivus. Collaborate comes from collaborare, 'to work together'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: collaborative 是 collaborate 加拉丁形容词词尾构成。collaborate 来自 collaborare「一起劳动」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor meant 'work, toil'. It is the noun that supplies the effort inside the word.
items.cn: labor 意为「劳动、辛苦」。它提供这个词内部的体力付出。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus laborare 'to work' gave collaborare 'to work together'.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 laborare「劳动」构成 collaborare「一起劳动」。

items.en: The ending -ivus marked 'tending to' or 'of the nature of'. English kept it in many adjectives such as active and creative.
items.cn: 词尾 -ivus 表示「倾向于」或「具有……性质」。英语在许多形容词里保留它，如 active 与 creative。

items.en: Collaborative appeared in English in the nineteenth century, first describing joint literary or scientific work.
items.cn: collaborative 在十九世纪出现于英语，最初描述共同的文学或科学工作。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective spread to teaching, management and design, where shared contribution became a stated goal.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个形容词扩展到教学、管理与设计，共享贡献成为明说的目标。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first printed use of collaborative is not precisely recorded, and the date when it became common in education is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：collaborative 最早印行于何时没有精确记录；它在教育领域普及的年代也无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from its own verb and from two words of different roots that also mean working together; group two holds the near synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组把这个形容词与它自己的动词、以及另外两个同表共同工作但词根不同的词分开；第二组是近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin cooperari, built on opus 'work'. It stresses readiness to help, not the shared design of a task.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cooperari，基底是 opus「工作」。它强调乐于相助，而非任务的共享设计。

entries.definition: From Latin collegium 'body of colleagues', built on legare 'to send'. It describes relations among peers, not joint production.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 collegium「同僚团体」，基底是 legare「派出」。它描述同侪关系，而非共同产出。

entries.definition: Built on legere 'to gather'; it stresses the group as a single body, while collaborative stresses the act of sharing work.
entries.definitionCN: 基底是 legere「收集」；它强调群体作为单一整体，而 collaborative 强调共同分担工作这一动作。

entries.definition: The activity itself; the adjective describes arrangements or people that have that activity as their character.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动本身；形容词则描述以这种活动为特征的安排或人。

entries.definition: Done by two or more parties together; it is neutral about how well they share.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同做出；不评价共享得好不好。

entries.definition: Held or used in common; it can describe a file, a flat or a belief without implying joint work.
entries.definitionCN: 共同持有或使用；可形容文件、公寓或信念，不必然含共同劳动。

entries.definition: Inviting people to take part in a process; participation can be consultation rather than shared authorship.
entries.definitionCN: 邀请人们参与过程；参与可以是咨询，而不必是共同创作。

entries.definition: Organized around teams; it describes the unit of work, while collaborative describes the manner of working.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕团队组织；它描述工作单位，collaborative 描述工作方式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Collaborate is the verb and collaborative the adjective, so the ending turns joint work into a quality.
normal.cn: collaborate 是动词，collaborative 是形容词，词尾把共同劳动变成性质。

normal.en: Laborare means work, so the adjective never loses the sense of effort.
normal.cn: laborare 意为劳动，所以这个形容词始终不丢「出力」的意思。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: collaborative research, collaborative learning, collaborative platform.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：协作研究、协作学习、协作平台。

normal.en: The word can describe a task's design or a person's temper, so check what it modifies.
normal.cn: 这个词既可描述任务设计，也可描述人的心性，要看它修饰什么。

normal.en: Cooperative and collegial look close but come from different roots and emphasize help or peers.
normal.cn: cooperative 与 collegial 看似相近，却来自不同词根，强调相助或同侪。

abstract.en: Picture several hands on one drawing, each line continued by the next hand.
abstract.cn: 想象几只手持同一张图，每条线都由下一只手接下去。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom where each group holds one piece of a puzzle.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，每组只拿到拼图的一块。

abstract.en: Picture a document that records every edit beside the name that made it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文档，每处修改旁都记下修改者的名字。

examples.en: The lab adopted a collaborative protocol for sharing instruments.
examples.cn: 实验室采用了一套共享仪器的协作规程。

examples.en: Collaborative learning changed who spoke first in the seminar.
examples.cn: 协作学习改变了研讨课上谁先发言。

examples.en: The platform is collaborative by design, not by accident.
examples.cn: 这个平台在设计上就是协作式的，而非偶然如此。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可 拉伯 瑞 提夫」——几只手的笔迹接在同一张图纸上 → 协作的

root: 拉丁 collaborare「一起劳动」+ 拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus；collaborare 由表示「一起」的成分加 laborare「劳动」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat the adjective as a structural mark, then apply it to research, learning, software, decision-making, the shared economy, personal temper and finally any design that assumes many hands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把这个形容词看作结构标记，再依次用于研究、学习、软件、决策、共享经济、个人心性，最后是任何在设计上假定有许多只手的安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single drawing on a long table with several hands editing the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌上一张图纸，几只不同的手在同一处改线。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND RESEARCH: the mark of many contributors, then the research project built around it.
branches.cn: 结构与研究：多方贡献的标记，再是围绕它建立的科研项目。

branches.en: LEARNING TOGETHER: knowledge is built between learners rather than delivered to them.
branches.cn: 共同学习：知识在学习者之间共建，而非被送达。

branches.en: SHARED SPACE AND MARKET: a common file, then a whole economy of shared platforms.
branches.cn: 共享空间与市场：先是共同文件，再是共享平台构成的整个经济。

branches.en: SHARED DECISION: affected parties help make the choice.
branches.cn: 共同决定：受影响各方参与作出选择。

branches.en: TEMPER AND DESIGN: a willingness to share credit, then any arrangement designed for many hands.
branches.cn: 心性与设计：愿共享功劳，以及任何为多只手设计的安排。

intro.en: Collaborative is a Latin verb of work plus a Latin adjective ending that English uses in hundreds of words.
intro.cn: collaborative 是一个表示劳动的拉丁动词，加一个英语用于数百个词的拉丁形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin laborare gives collaborate and collaboration; the adjective ending also appears in active, creative and competitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 laborare 衍生 collaborate 与 collaboration；这个形容词词尾也出现在 active、creative 与 competitive 中。

items.example: The verb names the act.

items.example: The ending turns the verb into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成性质。

items.example: The adjective describes the arrangement.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述安排。

definition_zh: 社会冲突；社会群体之间因利益、权力或价值分歧而发生的对抗
definition_en: open disagreement or struggle between social groups over interests, power or values
core_image: 广场两侧两队人举着不同的牌子，中间的空地越来越窄，喊声先把空气占满
scene: 一条街上的老住户与新开的店铺为了夜间噪音争了几个月，最后坐到同一张桌前。The social conflict over late-night noise ended only when both sides agreed to a curfew.
sceneCN: 这里 social conflict 指社会群体之间围绕利益或生活方式产生的对抗（第 1 个义项：群体间的冲突）；句意为围绕深夜噪音的社会冲突直到双方同意宵禁才结束。

pos.zh: 社会冲突（可数，指一场具体冲突；也可不可数，指冲突现象）
（社会学）群体间围绕资源、权力或价值的对抗状态

collocations.zh: 以阶级为基础的社会冲突

derivatives.zh: 冲突；抵触（由拉丁 conflictus「撞击、争斗」经古法语进入英语，保留「撞在一起」的意象）
相抵触的（由 conflict 加表示「进行」的后缀构成，转指同时成立却彼此不容）
冲突性的（由 conflict 加表示「性质」的后缀构成，转指以对抗为特征）
使痛苦；折磨（由表示「向」的拉丁前缀加 fligere「打击」构成，转指打击落到身上）
施加（痛苦、惩罚）（由表示「向内」的拉丁前缀加 fligere「打击」构成，转指把打击送进去）

senses.title: Conflict between social groups
senses.definition: open struggle between groups over interests, power, identity or values
senses.definitionCN: 群体之间围绕利益、权力、身份或价值发生的公开争斗
senses.example: The social conflict over late-night noise ended only when both sides agreed to a curfew.
senses.exampleCN: 围绕深夜噪音的社会冲突直到双方同意宵禁才结束。
senses.why: The phrase takes a general word for collision and gives it a subject: the colliding parties are groups, not individuals.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示「相撞」的一般词加上主语：相撞的是群体，不是个人。

senses.title: Class conflict
senses.definition: organised tension between social classes over wealth, work and political power
senses.definitionCN: 社会阶级之间围绕财富、劳动与政治权力的有组织张力
senses.example: Class conflict shaped the strikes of the early industrial city.
senses.exampleCN: 阶级冲突塑造了早期工业城市的罢工。
senses.why: Political economy narrowed the phrase to the fault line between owners and workers.
senses.whyCN: 政治经济学把这个短语收窄到所有者与劳动者之间的断层。

senses.title: Ethnic or cultural conflict
senses.definition: conflict between groups marked by language, religion, ethnicity or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 以语言、宗教、族群或生活方式划分的群体之间的冲突
senses.example: The social conflict in the border town was framed as cultural rather than economic.
senses.exampleCN: 边境小镇的社会冲突被解释为文化冲突，而非经济冲突。
senses.why: Identity joins interest here: groups may fight over what they are as much as over what they own.
senses.whyCN: 身份与利益在这里汇合：群体既可能为所有物争斗，也可能为「自己是谁」争斗。

senses.title: Conflict over resources
senses.definition: struggle over land, water, housing, jobs or other scarce goods
senses.definitionCN: 围绕土地、水源、住房、工作或其他稀缺物的争夺
senses.example: The social conflict over water sharpened as the reservoir fell.
senses.exampleCN: 随着水库水位下降，围绕水源的社会冲突加剧。
senses.why: Scarcity gives the phrase a material core: what is contested can be counted and divided.
senses.whyCN: 稀缺给这个短语一个物质内核：被争夺之物能被计数与分配。

senses.title: Conflict of norms and values
senses.definition: clash between groups whose ideas of right behaviour or a good life are incompatible
senses.definitionCN: 不同群体关于正当行为或好生活的观念彼此不容而产生的碰撞
senses.example: The social conflict was less about money than about how neighbours should live.
senses.exampleCN: 这场社会冲突与其说关乎钱，不如说关乎邻居应当如何生活。
senses.why: The word moves from goods to standards: what collides is not property but expectation.
senses.whyCN: 词义从物品移到标准：相撞的不是财产，而是期待。

senses.title: Conflict as a driver of change
senses.definition: conflict treated as a force that reshapes institutions rather than as a mere failure of order
senses.definitionCN: 被视为重塑制度的力量、而非仅仅秩序失败的那种冲突
senses.example: Social conflict over the vote forced the council to redraw its districts.
senses.exampleCN: 围绕投票权的社会冲突迫使议会重划选区。
senses.why: Sociology gave the word a positive reading: friction can be the mechanism by which a society adjusts.
senses.whyCN: 社会学给这个词一种正面读法：摩擦可以是社会自我调整的机制。

senses.title: Conflict management and resolution
senses.definition: the practices of containing, negotiating or settling a social conflict
senses.definitionCN: 控制、谈判或平息社会冲突的做法
senses.example: The city hired mediators trained in social conflict resolution.
senses.exampleCN: 市里聘用了受过社会冲突化解训练的中介人。
senses.why: Once conflict is seen as a process, it can be managed: the phrase becomes the name of a field of practice.
senses.whyCN: 一旦冲突被看作过程，它就可以被管理：这个短语成了一片实践领域的名称。

senses.title: Abstract: tension between social actors
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：社会行动者之间的张力
senses.definition: any unresolved tension between social actors, whether or not it has become open struggle
senses.definitionCN: 社会行动者之间任何未消解的张力，无论是否已经变成公开争斗
senses.example: A social conflict can remain latent for years before anyone marches.
senses.exampleCN: 一场社会冲突可以在无人上街之前潜伏多年。
senses.why: At its widest the phrase covers the quiet incompatibility that precedes any visible clash.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个短语涵盖任何可见冲突之前那种安静的不相容。

intro.en: Social conflict joins Latin socialis, 'of companions', to Latin conflictus, 'a collision, a contest', from confligere 'to strike together'. The compound is a modern social-science term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social conflict 把拉丁 socialis「同伴的」与拉丁 conflictus「撞击、争斗」接在一起，后者来自 confligere「撞在一起」。这个合成短语是现代社会科学术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fligere meant 'to strike, dash'. It is the verb of impact behind conflict, afflict and inflict.
items.cn: fligere 意为「打击、猛撞」。它是 conflict、afflict 与 inflict 背后的撞击动词。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus fligere produced confligere 'to strike together, contend, fight'.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 fligere 构成 confligere「撞在一起、争斗、作战」。

items.en: Conflictus named a collision or a contest; English conflict entered through Old French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: conflictus 指撞击或争斗；英语 conflict 在十四世纪经古法语进入。

items.en: Nineteenth-century political and social theory joined the word to social to name struggle between classes, nations or groups.
items.cn: 十九世纪的政治与社会理论把这个词与 social 结合，命名阶级、民族或群体之间的争斗。

items.en: Twentieth-century sociology made social conflict theory a named approach, treating conflict as a normal part of social structure.
items.cn: 二十世纪社会学把冲突理论变成一个有名目的路径，将冲突视为社会结构的正常部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first printed use of the exact compound is not recorded, and the boundary between the resource and value senses is often blurred in the literature.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个确切合成短语最早印行于何时没有记录；资源义与价值义在文献中的边界常被模糊处理。

note.en: Group one separates the compound from the bare word and from two verbs of the same striking root; group two holds neighbours for open struggle.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与单纯的冲突词、以及两个同出「打击」词根的动词分开；第二组是公开争斗的近邻词。

entries.definition: Collision or disagreement in general; the compound specifies that the parties are social groups.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指撞击或分歧；合成短语则指明各方是社会群体。

entries.definition: To cause pain or trouble; the root idea of striking is aimed at a sufferer, not at a contest between groups.
entries.definitionCN: 造成痛苦或困扰；词根的「打击」指向受苦者，而非群体间的争斗。

entries.definition: To impose pain or punishment on someone; it is one-way, while conflict is mutual.
entries.definitionCN: 把痛苦或惩罚加于某人；它是单向的，而冲突是相互的。

entries.definition: From Latin vincere 'to conquer'; it means to find guilty, with no sense of social struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vincere「征服」；意为判定有罪，没有社会争斗义。

entries.definition: A disagreement expressed in words, often between individuals or over a specific matter.
entries.definitionCN: 用言语表达的分歧，常在个人之间或围绕具体事项。

entries.definition: Strained relations that may not yet be open; it is the quiet stage of a conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未公开的紧张关系；它是冲突的安静阶段。

entries.definition: Bitter, prolonged conflict, often within a community; it carries a stronger tone than the neutral compound.
entries.definitionCN: 激烈而持久的冲突，常在共同体内部；语气比中性的合成短语更强。

entries.definition: Collective dissatisfaction that may produce protests or disorder; it is a symptom that can precede conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 可能引发抗议或骚乱的集体不满；它可以是冲突的前兆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Fligere means strike, so conflict is a striking together of two forces.
normal.cn: fligere 意为打击，所以 conflict 是两股力量撞在一起。

normal.en: The social half names the parties: not two people, but groups with a shared position.
normal.cn: social 这一半命名各方：不是两个人，而是有共同立场的群体。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the causes: over resources, over values, class-based.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出起因：围绕资源、围绕价值、以阶级为基础。

normal.en: The same striking root gives afflict and inflict, both one-way forms of harm.
normal.cn: 同一个「打击」词根衍生 afflict 与 inflict，两者都是单向伤害。

normal.en: Conflict theory treats the compound as normal structure, not simply as breakdown.
normal.cn: 冲突理论把这个短语当作正常结构，而非单纯的崩溃。

abstract.en: Picture two crowds pressing toward a narrow strip of pavement from opposite sides.
abstract.cn: 想象两群人从相反方向挤向一条窄窄的人行道。

abstract.en: Picture a fault line under a town that only shows when the ground moves.
abstract.cn: 想象镇下一条断层，只在地面移动时才显出来。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks in one room never agreeing on the hour.
abstract.cn: 想象同一间屋里两只钟，报时永远不一致。

examples.en: The housing shortage turned a quiet social conflict into open protest.
examples.cn: 住房短缺把一场安静的社会冲突变成公开抗议。

examples.en: Conflict theory treats social conflict as a normal feature of institutions.
examples.cn: 冲突理论把社会冲突视为制度的正常特征。

examples.en: Mediators were called in to manage the social conflict over the market site.
examples.cn: 调解人被请来管理围绕市场选址的社会冲突。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜秀 康 弗利克特」——社会两方撞在一起 → 社会冲突

root: 拉丁 socialis「同伴的」+ 拉丁 conflictus「撞击、争斗」；conflictus 来自 confligere「撞在一起」，其基底 fligere 意为「打击」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with open struggle between groups, then move through class, identity, resources, values, conflict as change, conflict management and finally latent tension.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从群体间的公开争斗出发，经过阶级、身份、资源、价值，再到作为变迁动力的冲突、冲突管理，最后是潜伏的张力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two crowds pressing from opposite sides toward one narrow strip of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：两群人从相反方向挤向同一条窄地。

branches.en: WHO AND WHAT: groups collide, and the first thing they collide over is a scarce resource.
branches.cn: 谁与什么：群体相撞，最先撞上的是稀缺资源。

branches.en: CLASS AND CHANGE: owners against workers, and friction as the mechanism of adjustment.
branches.cn: 阶级与变迁：所有者对劳动者，摩擦成为调整机制。

branches.en: IDENTITY AND STANDARDS: what a group is, and how it believes people should live.
branches.cn: 身份与标准：群体是什么，以及它认为人应当如何生活。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: once conflict is a process, it can be negotiated and settled.
branches.cn: 管理：冲突一旦成为过程，就可以谈判与平息。

branches.en: LATENT TENSION: the quiet incompatibility before any visible clash.
branches.cn: 潜伏张力：任何可见冲突之前的安静不相容。

intro.en: Social conflict joins a Latin adjective of companionship to a Latin noun of collision.
intro.cn: social conflict 把一个表示同伴关系的拉丁形容词接上一个表示撞击的拉丁名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius gives social and society; Latin fligere gives conflict, afflict and inflict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 social 与 society；拉丁 fligere 衍生 conflict、afflict 与 inflict。

items.example: The first word names the parties.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词命名各方。

items.example: Socialis became English social.
items.exampleCN: socialis 成为英语 social。

items.example: The second word begins with impact.
items.exampleCN: 第二个词从撞击开始。

items.example: The prefix makes the strike mutual.
items.exampleCN: 前缀让打击成为相互的。

items.structure: confligere plus a noun of action
items.example: Conflictus names the clash.
items.exampleCN: conflictus 命名碰撞。

items.example: English shortened the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语缩短了这个拉丁名词。

items.structure: conflict plus a suffix of ongoing action
items.example: Two claims can be conflicting.
items.exampleCN: 两种主张可以彼此抵触。

items.example: Afflict is the one-way strike.
items.exampleCN: afflict 是单向的打击。

items.example: Inflict sends the blow inward.
items.exampleCN: inflict 把打击送进去。

definition_zh: 团结；群体成员因共同处境或共同目标而相互支持、彼此承担
definition_en: the unity and mutual support of people who share a common situation or aim
core_image: 码头工人排成一列，把手里的工具传给下一个人，谁也没有多拿，队伍却一直不断
scene: 洪水退去后，邻村的人带着抽水机和干粮赶来，不问谁家先被淹。Solidarity across the valley brought pumps and food before any official order arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 solidarity 指群体成员因共同处境而相互支持的团结（第 1 个义项：共享目标下的联合）；句意为跨谷的团结在任何官方命令到达之前就送来了抽水机与食物。

pos.zh: 团结；相互支持（不可数，指关系或精神状态）
不同类型的团结（用复数 solidarities，见于社会学讨论）

derivatives.zh: 坚固的；实心的；固体（由拉丁 solidus「坚实、完整」直接借入）
坚固性；可靠性（由 solid 加表示「性质」的后缀构成，从物理坚实转指关系可靠）
使凝固；使巩固（由 solid 加表示「使成为」的后缀构成，转指由松散变为坚实）
巩固；合并（由表示「完全」的拉丁前缀加 solidus 构成，转指把分散之物压成一体）
士兵（由拉丁 solidus「金币」衍生晚期拉丁「领饷者」，从军饷转指拿饷打仗的人）
焊接；焊料（由拉丁 solidare「使坚实」经古法语进入英语，转指用金属把接缝变实）

senses.title: Unity around shared aims
senses.definition: the state in which people with a common aim support one another and accept shared responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 有共同目标的人彼此支持、共同承担的状态
senses.example: Solidarity across the valley brought pumps and food before any official order arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 跨谷的团结在任何官方命令到达之前就送来了抽水机与食物。
senses.why: The word names a bond created by a shared condition, not by a contract: people stand together because they are in the same situation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名由共同处境而非契约造出的纽带：人们站在一起，因为处境相同。

senses.title: Mutual support among workers
senses.definition: the organised mutual support of workers, especially through unions and strikes
senses.definitionCN: 劳动者有组织的相互支持，尤指通过工会与罢工
senses.example: The strike held because solidarity kept other depots from moving the goods.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工得以维持，是因为团结让其他仓库不肯运货。
senses.why: Labour movements gave the word its strongest modern use: support that costs the supporter something.
senses.whyCN: 工人运动给这个词最强的现代用法：支持者自己要付出代价的那种支持。

senses.title: Solidarity as a moral duty
senses.definition: a moral obligation to stand with others who suffer, even when one gains nothing
senses.definitionCN: 与他人共处困境、即使自己无所得也应当站在一起的道德义务
senses.example: She joined the vigil out of solidarity rather than curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她参加守夜是出于团结，而非好奇。
senses.why: Here the bond becomes a duty: the question is not whether one benefits, but whether one owes support.
senses.whyCN: 这里纽带变成责任：问题不是自己是否受益，而是自己是否应当支持。

senses.title: International solidarity
senses.definition: support across borders for people facing disaster, repression or war
senses.definitionCN: 跨越国界、对遭受灾难、压制或战争的人的支持
senses.example: Aid arrived under the banner of international solidarity.
senses.exampleCN: 援助打着国际团结的旗号到达。
senses.why: The word crosses borders when suffering is treated as a common human condition rather than a national matter.
senses.whyCN: 当苦难被视为共同的人类处境而非一国之事，这个词就跨过国界。

senses.title: Community cohesion
senses.definition: the everyday ties that hold a neighbourhood or village together
senses.definitionCN: 把邻里或村庄拢在一起的日常纽带
senses.example: The annual feast is the village's main expression of solidarity.
senses.exampleCN: 一年一度的宴席是村里团结的主要表达。
senses.why: Community studies use the word for the quiet, repeated acts that make a place hold together.
senses.whyCN: 社区研究用这个词指让一个地方维持不散的安静而重复的行动。

senses.title: The social-insurance solidarity principle
senses.titleCN: 社会保险中的互助原则
senses.definition: the principle that contributors pool risk so that those in need are supported by all
senses.definitionCN: 缴费者共担风险、使有需要者由全体支持的原则
senses.example: Health insurance rests on solidarity, not on individual savings alone.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗保险依靠互助，而不只是个人储蓄。
senses.why: Welfare systems borrowed the word for pooled risk: the healthy support the sick, the young support the old.
senses.whyCN: 福利制度借用这个词表示风险共担：健康者支持病者，年轻者支持年长者。

senses.title: Solidarity with a cause
senses.definition: public support for a group or cause one does not belong to
senses.definitionCN: 对并非自己所属的群体或事业给予的公开支持
senses.example: Writers signed the letter in solidarity with the imprisoned journalists.
senses.exampleCN: 作家们签署这封信，声援被囚的记者。
senses.why: The word can reach outward: one need not share the condition in order to stand with those who endure it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以向外延伸：不必共享处境，也可以站在承受者一边。

senses.title: Abstract: a bond from shared condition
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：共同处境造就的纽带
senses.definition: any bond that arises because people share a condition, risk or fate
senses.definitionCN: 因人们共享处境、风险或命运而产生的任何纽带
senses.example: Solidarity can appear among strangers waiting in the same flooded street.
senses.exampleCN: 团结可以出现在同一条被淹街道上等候的陌生人之间。
senses.why: At its widest the word names the invisible thread that a shared condition spins between people.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个词命名共同处境在人与人之间纺出的那根看不见的线。

intro.en: Solidarity comes from French solidarité, built on solidaire 'interdependent', from Latin solidus 'solid, whole'. The political sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solidarity 来自法语 solidarité，其基底 solidaire 意为「相互依存的」，再追溯到拉丁 solidus「坚实、完整」。政治义是十九世纪的产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solidus meant 'firm, whole, entire'. It also named a Roman gold coin, which is why soldier and solder belong to the same family.
items.cn: solidus 意为「坚实、完整、整个」。它也是一种罗马金币的名称，因此 soldier 与 solder 同属这一词族。

items.en: The root behind solidus is usually reconstructed as a Indo-European form meaning 'whole'. This is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: solidus 背后的词根通常被重构为一个意为「完整」的印欧形式。这是重构形式，并非有文献记录的词。

items.en: French solidaire meant 'jointly responsible, interdependent', describing people whose obligations are linked.
items.cn: 法语 solidaire 意为「连带负责的、相互依存的」，描述义务彼此相连的人。

items.en: Solidarité named the state of being jointly responsible; it is generally dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: solidarité 命名「连带负责」的状态；一般认为它出现在十九世纪。

items.en: English solidarity entered through political and labour writing, where it named support that binds workers or nations.
items.cn: 英语 solidarity 经政治与工人运动写作进入，命名把劳动者或国家绑在一起的支援。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact first French and English uses are not recorded, and the pre-Latin root of solidus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：法语与英语的最早用例没有记录；solidus 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one keeps the 'firm, whole' family together with a coin-derived relative; group two holds words for unity and support.
note.cn: 第一组把「坚实、完整」词族的词与一个由金币义衍生的亲属词放在一起；第二组是联合与支持的同义词。

entries.definition: Firm and whole in a physical sense; solidarity applies that firmness to relations between people.
entries.definitionCN: 物理意义上的坚实与完整；solidarity 把这种坚实用于人与人的关系。

entries.definition: The quality of being physically solid or reliable; it names a property, not a social bond.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上坚实或可靠的属性；它命名属性，不命名社会纽带。

entries.definition: To press separate things into one firm body; solidarity is the resulting social bond, not the act of pressing.
entries.definitionCN: 把分散之物压成一个坚实的整体；solidarity 是形成的社会纽带，而非压的动作。

entries.definition: From Late Latin solidarius 'one serving for pay', from solidus as a coin. It is a relative by way of money, not of unity.
entries.definitionCN: 来自晚期拉丁 solidarius「领饷服役者」，其 solidus 指金币。它经由钱而非经由团结与这个词同族。

entries.definition: The state of being one whole; solidarity adds mutual support and shared responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 成为一个整体的状态；solidarity 还加上相互支持与共同责任。

entries.definition: The force that keeps a group together; it can be measured, while solidarity is also a moral stance.
entries.definitionCN: 把群体拢在一起的力量；它可被测量，而 solidarity 也是一种道德立场。

entries.definition: Warm friendship among people who share an activity; it is lighter and more personal than solidarity.
entries.definitionCN: 共享活动者之间温暖的友情；它比 solidarity 更轻、更私人。

entries.definition: People helping one another in practice, often through organised networks; solidarity is the bond that motivates such aid.
entries.definitionCN: 人们在实践中互相帮助，常通过有组织的网络；solidarity 是推动这种援助的纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Solidus meant whole and firm, so solidarity is a group holding together as one body.
normal.cn: solidus 意为完整而坚实，所以 solidarity 是一个群体作为一个整体抱在一起。

normal.en: French solidaire means jointly responsible, which is why the word is about obligations, not only feelings.
normal.cn: 法语 solidaire 意为连带负责，所以这个词关乎义务，不只是感情。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the direction: in solidarity with, show solidarity, international solidarity.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示方向：声援、表示团结、国际团结。

normal.en: The same root gives consolidate, which makes separate things firm as one.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 consolidate，把分散之物压成坚实的一体。

normal.en: Soldier belongs by way of the gold coin solidus, a relative through money rather than unity.
normal.cn: soldier 经由金币 solidus 同族，是同过钱而非同过团结的亲属。

abstract.en: Picture dock workers passing tools down a line, nobody taking more than needed.
abstract.cn: 想象码头工人把工具沿队伍传下去，谁也没有多拿。

abstract.en: Picture strangers in a flooded street forming a chain without being asked.
abstract.cn: 想象被淹街道上的陌生人不用谁招呼就拉成一条链。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose every plank carries part of the weight of the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，每块板都承担下一块的一部分重量。

examples.en: Neighbours brought generators in solidarity after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，邻居们出于团结送来发电机。

examples.en: The union called for solidarity with the locked-out workers.
examples.cn: 工会呼吁声援被拒之门外的工人。

examples.en: Health systems rely on solidarity between the healthy and the ill.
examples.cn: 医疗体系依靠健康者与病者之间的互助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「索里 达 瑞提」——大家抱成一个完整坚实的整体 → 团结

root: 法语 solidarité「连带责任」← solidaire「相互依存的」← 拉丁 solidus「坚实、完整」；solidus 更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with unity around a shared aim, then move to workers, moral duty, international support, community ties, pooled risk, support for a cause and finally any bond made by a shared condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从围绕共同目标的联合出发，经过劳动者、道德责任、国际支援、社区纽带、风险共担、对事业的声援，最后是任何由共同处境造就的纽带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people passing a heavy tool hand to hand, no one keeping it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列人把沉重的工具一手传一手，谁都不把它留下。

branches.en: THE BOND AND THE VILLAGE: unity around an aim, and the quiet daily ties that hold a place together.
branches.cn: 纽带与村庄：围绕目标的联合，以及把地方拢住的安静日常纽带。

branches.en: ORGANISED SUPPORT: workers acting through unions, and contributors pooling risk in insurance.
branches.cn: 有组织的支持：劳动者通过工会行动，缴费者在保险中风险共担。

branches.en: DUTY AND CAUSE: support owed to those who suffer, and support offered to those one does not belong to.
branches.cn: 责任与事业：对受苦者应尽的支援，以及对非所属群体的公开声援。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: suffering treated as a common human condition.
branches.cn: 跨越国界：苦难被视为共同的人类处境。

branches.en: THE THREAD: the widest reading names the invisible bond that a shared condition spins.
branches.cn: 那根线：最宽的读法命名共同处境纺出的看不见的纽带。

intro.en: Solidarity is a French social noun built on a Latin adjective of firmness and wholeness.
intro.cn: solidarity 是一个法语社会名词，其基底是表示坚实与完整的拉丁形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin solidus gives solid, solidity, consolidate and soldier; French solidaire gives solidarity and solidary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solidus 衍生 solid、solidity、consolidate 与 soldier；法语 solidaire 衍生 solidarity 与 solidary。

items.example: The root carries firmness and completeness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着坚实与完整。

items.example: Solid keeps the physical sense.
items.exampleCN: solid 保留物理义。

items.structure: solid plus a suffix of quality
items.example: Solidity names the property.
items.exampleCN: solidity 命名属性。

items.example: Consolidate presses separate parts together.
items.exampleCN: consolidate 把分散部分压到一起。

items.meaningCN: 连带负责的；相互依存的
items.example: Solidaire adds obligation to firmness.
items.exampleCN: solidaire 在坚实之上加上义务。

items.structure: solidaire plus a suffix of state
items.example: The noun names the social bond.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名社会纽带。

items.example: Solidary describes the relation.
items.exampleCN: solidary 描述这种关系。

items.structure: Late Latin solidarius, from solidus as pay
items.example: The coin sense produced the fighter.
items.exampleCN: 金币义衍生出战士。

items.example: Solder makes a joint solid.

latinEntries.structure: solidus, solida, solidum (adjective); solidus, solidi (m. noun)

definition_zh: 教育工作者；教师；从事教育、尤其研究教育方法的人
definition_en: a person whose work is teaching, training or studying how people are educated
core_image: 一个人蹲下来与学生视线齐平，把同一道题换三种说法，直到对方眼睛亮起来
scene: 乡村学校的老师放学后留下来，把不会读的孩子一个个叫到身边，从字母的声音重新开始。The educator stayed after class to rebuild each struggling reader's confidence.
sceneCN: 这里 educator 指以教学与育人为职业的人（第 1 个义项：教育工作者）；句意为这位教育工作者放学后留下来，帮助每个阅读困难的孩子重建信心。

pos.zh: 教育工作者；教师（较 teacher 正式，常含专业训练之意）
教育研究者或教育理论工作者

derivatives.zh: 教育；培养（由拉丁 educare「养育、培养」进入英语，保留「把人带大」的动作义）
教育；教育学（由 educate 加表示「动作」的后缀构成，转指培养的过程与制度）
教育的；有教育意义的（由 education 加表示「属于」的后缀构成）
有教育作用的（由 educate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指能带来教益）
引出；使显现（由拉丁 educere「引出」进入英语，与 educate 同源但义不同）

senses.title: A professional teacher
senses.definition: a person trained and employed to teach, usually in a school or college
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、受雇从事教学的人，通常在学校或学院工作
senses.example: The educator stayed after class to rebuild each struggling reader's confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这位教育工作者放学后留下来，帮助每个阅读困难的孩子重建信心。
senses.why: The word is the agent noun of educate: it names the person whose work is the act, and it sounds more professional than teacher.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 educate 的动作执行者名词：它命名以这一动作为职业的人，听来比 teacher 更专业。

senses.title: An instructor of a skill
senses.definition: someone who teaches a practical skill outside a formal school, such as a coach or workshop leader
senses.definitionCN: 在正式学校之外传授实用技艺的人，如教练或工作坊带领者
senses.example: The centre hired an educator to teach safe kitchen practice.
senses.exampleCN: 中心聘请了一位教育人员来教安全厨房操作。
senses.why: Once the setting leaves the classroom, the word widens from subject teaching to demonstrated practice.
senses.whyCN: 一旦场景离开教室，这个词就从学科教学扩展到示范性实践。

senses.title: A theorist of education
senses.definition: a person who studies how learning works and proposes how teaching should be organised
senses.definitionCN: 研究学习如何发生、并提出教学应如何组织的人
senses.example: The conference brought educators and psychologists into one room.
senses.exampleCN: 会议把教育理论家与心理学家聚到同一间屋里。
senses.why: The same noun covers the person who teaches and the person who studies teaching, because both work on the act of educating.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既覆盖教书的人，也覆盖研究教学的人，因为两者都作用于「教育」这一动作。

senses.title: A museum or health educator
senses.titleCN: 博物馆或健康教育工作者
senses.definition: a specialist who designs exhibits, programmes or campaigns so that the public learns something
senses.definitionCN: 设计展览、项目或宣传活动以使公众学到东西的专职人员
senses.example: The museum educator rewrote every label for younger visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆教育员为年幼参观者重写了每块说明牌。
senses.why: Public institutions created new educator roles: the work is teaching, but the classroom is a hall or a clinic.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构创造了新的教育者岗位：工作仍是教学，但教室成了展厅或诊所。

senses.title: An educator who shapes values
senses.definition: a person who guides not only knowledge but also character and conduct
senses.definitionCN: 不仅引导知识、也引导品格与行为的人
senses.example: Her old teacher remained an educator in the moral sense long after retirement.
senses.exampleCN: 她的老师退休很久之后，仍在道德意义上是一位育人者。
senses.why: The word can carry the older sense of bringing a person up, not merely instructing them in a subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以带着更古老的「把人带大」义，而不只是教授一门学科。

senses.title: An early childhood educator
senses.definition: a trained person who works with young children's development through play and routine
senses.definitionCN: 通过游戏与日常作息促进幼儿发展的专业人员
senses.example: The nursery employs one early childhood educator for every four children.
senses.exampleCN: 这家托儿所为每四个孩子配备一名幼儿教育工作者。
senses.why: Professional titles narrowed the word into a recognised occupation with its own training and standards.
senses.whyCN: 专业职衔把这个词收窄为一个有自身培训与标准的公认职业。

senses.title: A corporate trainer
senses.definition: a person paid by an organisation to develop employees' skills or conduct
senses.definitionCN: 受组织聘用、负责培养员工技能或行为的人
senses.example: The bank's educator runs weekly sessions on handling complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行的教育人员每周开设处理投诉的课程。
senses.why: Business borrowed the school word for adult training, keeping the teaching function but changing the subject to work.
senses.whyCN: 企业借用学校里的词来指成人培训，保留教学功能，却把科目换成工作。

senses.title: Abstract: anyone who shapes understanding
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何塑造理解的人
senses.definition: any person or thing that helps someone understand something better
senses.definitionCN: 任何帮助某人更好地理解某事的个人或事物
senses.example: A good editor is an educator in disguise.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好的编辑是伪装的教育者。
senses.why: At its widest the noun leaves the profession behind and names the role of helping another mind change.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个名词离开职业，命名帮助另一个心智发生改变的角色。

intro.en: Educator is the Latin agent noun of educare 'to bring up, rear'. Educare is related to educere 'to lead out', from ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: educator 是拉丁 educare「养育、培养」的动作执行者名词。educare 与 educere「引出」相关，后者由表示「向外」的成分加 ducere「引导」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. It is the verb behind duct, conduct, introduce and reduce.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」。它是 duct、conduct、introduce 与 reduce 背后的动词。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ducere produced educere 'to lead out', the image of drawing a person out of ignorance.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的成分加 ducere 构成 educere「引出」，意象是把人从无知中拉出来。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is closely related to educere, and the two verbs were already linked in Latin.
items.cn: educare 意为「养育、抚养、培养」。它与 educere 关系密切，两个动词在拉丁语中已经彼此关联。

items.en: Educator was the Latin noun for a tutor or one who brings another up, and English took it as a formal name for a teacher.
items.cn: educator 是拉丁语中指导师或抚养者的名词，英语把它接受为教师的正式称呼。

items.en: English educator is recorded from the sixteenth century, and it long meant a person who trains the young rather than an academic theorist.
items.cn: 英语 educator 自十六世纪有记录，长期指培养年轻人的人，而非教育理论家。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the precise first English use is not recorded, and the relationship between educare and educere is explained differently by different etymologists.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语最早用例没有精确记录；不同词源学家对 educare 与 educere 的关系有不同解释。

note.en: Group one separates the agent noun from its own verb family and from one look-alike of a different root; group two holds the everyday names for teaching roles.
note.cn: 第一组把这个动作执行者名词与它自己的动词词族、以及一个异源形近词分开；第二组是教学角色的日常名称。

entries.definition: The process or system of educating; the educator is the person who carries it out.
entries.definitionCN: 教育的过程或制度；educator 是执行它的人。

entries.definition: Producing learning or insight; it describes an experience, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 能带来学习或洞见；它描述经验，不描述人。

entries.definition: To draw out something hidden; it shares the 'lead out' image but names the act, not the profession.
entries.definitionCN: 把隐藏之物引出来；它共享「引出」意象，却命名动作，不命名职业。

entries.definition: From Latin edere 'to give out', built on dare 'to give', not ducere. It means a published version.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 edere「发出」，基底是 dare「给」，并非 ducere；它指出版物的一种版本。

entries.definition: The plain, everyday name for a person who teaches; educator is more formal and often implies training or policy.
entries.definitionCN: 教人者的日常称呼；educator 更正式，常含专业训练或政策意味。

entries.definition: A person who instructs in a particular skill or course; educator is broader and can include theory.
entries.definitionCN: 在特定技能或课程中指导的人；educator 更宽，也可包括理论工作。

entries.definition: A person who trains others in a job or sport; the setting is practical rather than academic.
entries.definitionCN: 在工作或运动中训练他人的人；场景偏实践，而非学术。

entries.definition: A person who teaches an individual or a small group; educator can name the whole profession.
entries.definitionCN: 教一个人或一个小组的人；educator 可命名整个职业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ducere means lead, so an educator is one who leads another out of ignorance.
normal.cn: ducere 意为引导，所以 educator 是把另一个人从无知中引出来的人。

normal.en: The agent ending marks the person: the verb educates, the noun names who does it.
normal.cn: 表示执行者的词尾标出人：动词是 educate，名词命名做这件事的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: professional educator, early childhood educator, museum educator.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：专业教育工作者、幼儿教育工作者、博物馆教育员。

normal.en: The same family gives education and educational, keeping the process rather than the person.
normal.cn: 同一词族衍生 education 与 educational，保留过程而非人。

normal.en: Educe shares the 'lead out' image but means drawing something hidden into view.
normal.cn: educe 共享「引出」意象，却指把隐藏之物引到可见处。

abstract.en: Picture an adult kneeling so that their eyes are level with a child's.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大人蹲下来，使自己的视线与孩子齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room where someone slowly opens the door from the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一间锁着的屋子，有人从里面慢慢把门打开。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at a letter again and again until its sound finally appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手一遍遍指向一个字母，直到它的声音终于出现。

examples.en: The district hired an educator to redesign its reading programme.
examples.cn: 学区聘请了一位教育工作者来重新设计阅读项目。

examples.en: A museum educator turned the storage room into a teaching space.
examples.cn: 一位博物馆教育员把库房变成教学空间。

examples.en: The award honoured an educator who had taught three generations.
examples.cn: 该奖项表彰了一位教过三代人的教育工作者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一丢 凯 特」——把人从无知里引出来的人 → 教育工作者

root: 拉丁 educare「养育、培养」的动作执行者名词；educare 与 educere「引出」相关，后者 = 表示「向外」的成分 + ducere「引导」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the trained teacher, then widen to skill instructors, theorists, public educators, character guides, early childhood specialists, corporate trainers and finally anyone who changes another mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从受过训练的教师出发，再扩展到技艺传授者、理论家、公共教育者、品格引导者、幼教专家、企业培训者，最后是任何改变另一个心智的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an adult kneels to a child's eye level and tries a third way of explaining.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个大人蹲到孩子的视线高度，换第三种说法再讲一次。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: the trained teacher, and the early childhood specialist with their own standards.
branches.cn: 职业：受过训练的教师，以及有自身标准的幼教专家。

branches.en: BEYOND THE SCHOOL: a skill instructor outside class, and a trainer inside a company.
branches.cn: 学校之外：课堂外的技艺传授者，以及企业内的培训者。

branches.en: THEORY AND THE HALL: the person who studies teaching, and the person who teaches in a museum or clinic.
branches.cn: 理论与实践场：研究教学的人，以及在展厅或诊所教学的人。

branches.en: CHARACTER: the educator who guides conduct, not only knowledge.
branches.cn: 品格：不仅引导知识、也引导行为的育人者。

branches.en: THE ROLE ITSELF: anyone or anything that helps another mind change.
branches.cn: 角色本身：任何帮助另一个心智发生改变的人或事物。

intro.en: Educator is a Latin verb of leading and rearing, with an agent ending that names the person who does it.
intro.cn: educator 是一个表示引导与养育的拉丁动词，加上一个命名执行者的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct, introduce, reduce and educe; educare gives educate, education and educator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educe；educare 衍生 educate、education 与 educator。

items.example: The root supplies the leading.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「引导」。

items.example: Educere draws a person out.
items.exampleCN: educere 把人引出来。

items.example: Educare adds nurture to leading.
items.exampleCN: educare 在引导之上加上养育。

items.example: Educate is the act.
items.exampleCN: educate 是动作。

items.structure: educate plus a suffix of action
items.example: Education names the process.
items.exampleCN: education 命名过程。

items.structure: educate plus a suffix meaning 'person who acts'
items.example: The agent ending names the person.
items.exampleCN: 执行者词尾命名人。

items.example: Educational describes the field.
items.exampleCN: educational 描述这一领域。

items.structure: educate plus an adjective ending of tendency
items.example: Educative describes an effect.
items.exampleCN: educative 描述效果。

items.meaning: to draw out what is hidden
items.example: Educe keeps the 'out' image without the school.
items.exampleCN: educe 保留「引出」意象，却不含学校。

definition_zh: 教育；培养；训练；向公众普及知识
definition_en: to teach, train or develop someone's knowledge, skill and judgment
core_image: 一个人牵着孩子的手，从黑暗的屋子一步步走到门口，门外的光是孩子自己看见的
scene: 博物馆把库房里的标本搬到走廊，让孩子可以伸手触摸并提问。The museum uses its corridor exhibits to educate visitors about local wildlife.
sceneCN: 这里 educate 指向公众传授知识、培养理解（第 3 个义项：向公众普及）；句意为博物馆用走廊展品向参观者普及本地野生动植物知识。

pos.zh: 教育；培养；训练（可指学校教育，也可指培养判断力）
向公众普及；告知（常与 public、consumers 等搭配）

derivatives.zh: 教育；教育学（由 educate 加表示「动作」的后缀构成，转指培养的过程与制度）
教育工作者（由 educate 加表示「执行者」的后缀构成，转指以教育为职业的人）
教育的；有教育意义的（由 education 加表示「属于」的后缀构成）
有教育作用的（由 educate 加表示「倾向」的后缀构成，转指能带来教益）
引出；使显现（由拉丁 educere「引出」进入英语，与 educate 同源但义不同）

senses.title: To teach in school
senses.definition: to provide formal instruction, usually in a school or college
senses.definitionCN: 通常在学校或学院提供正式教学
senses.example: The school educates children from six to sixteen.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校教育六岁到十六岁的孩子。
senses.why: This is the everyday school sense: an institution and a curriculum carry the act.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的学校义：机构与课程承载这一动作。

senses.title: To bring up and nurture
senses.definition: to care for a person's growth and character over time, not only their knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 长期照料一个人的成长与品格，而不只是知识
senses.example: Her grandmother educated her in patience as much as in letters.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母教她认字，也教她耐心。
senses.why: The Latin verb began with rearing, and this older sense survives whenever the object is a whole person.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词最初指养育，只要宾语是完整的人，这层古老义就仍在。

senses.title: To inform the public
senses.definition: to help a broad audience understand an issue, often through campaigns, exhibits or media
senses.definitionCN: 通过宣传活动、展览或媒体帮助广泛受众理解某一议题
senses.example: The museum uses its corridor exhibits to educate visitors about local wildlife.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆用走廊展品向参观者普及本地野生动植物知识。
senses.why: The object widens from a pupil to the public, and the verb becomes a form of public communication.
senses.whyCN: 宾语从学生扩到公众，这个动词就变成一种公共传播。

senses.title: To train in a skill
senses.definition: to develop practical ability through instruction and practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过指导与练习发展实际能力
senses.example: The course educates new staff in safe handling of chemicals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程训练新员工安全处理化学品。
senses.why: Skill training narrows the verb from general development to a demonstrable competence.
senses.whyCN: 技能训练把这个动词从一般发展收窄到可演示的能力。

senses.title: To cultivate taste or judgment
senses.definition: to refine someone's ability to notice, compare and decide
senses.definitionCN: 提升某人察觉、比较与判断的能力
senses.example: Travel educated his eye for architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行培养了他对建筑的眼光。
senses.why: The verb can take an inner faculty as its object, so education becomes the training of perception.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以拿内在能力作宾语，教育于是成为感知的训练。

senses.title: To inform consumers
senses.definition: to give buyers information so that they can choose or use a product responsibly
senses.definitionCN: 向买家提供信息，使其能负责地选择或使用产品
senses.example: The label educates consumers about where the beans were grown.
senses.exampleCN: 标签告知消费者咖啡豆的产地。
senses.why: Business uses the word for disclosure: the seller teaches, though often within a marketing frame.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这个词表示信息披露：卖方在教，尽管常在营销框架内。

senses.title: To educate oneself
senses.definition: to pursue knowledge or skill without being taught by an institution
senses.definitionCN: 不经机构教学而自行追求知识或技能
senses.example: He educated himself in law while working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 他上夜班时自学法律。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the verb inward: the same person is both teacher and learner.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把这个动词转向内部：同一个人既是教师也是学习者。

senses.title: Abstract: to lead out of ignorance
senses.definition: to help someone move from not knowing to knowing, whatever the method
senses.definitionCN: 以任何方式帮助某人从不知走向知
senses.example: A single good question can educate more than a long lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题有时比一堂长讲座更能教育人。
senses.why: At its most abstract the verb names the movement of a mind, not a classroom or a syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个动词命名心智的移动，而非教室或大纲。

intro.en: Educate comes from Latin educare 'to bring up, rear', closely related to educere 'to lead out' (ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead'). It entered English in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: educate 来自拉丁 educare「养育、培养」，与 educere「引出」关系密切，后者由表示「向外」的成分加 ducere「引导」构成。它在十五世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. Its family includes conduct, introduce, reduce and produce.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」。其词族包括 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 produce。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ducere gave educere 'to lead out'. The image is drawing a person out of ignorance rather than filling them.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的成分加 ducere 构成 educere「引出」。意象是把人从无知中拉出来，而非往里面填东西。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is a related verb, and Latin writers already used it alongside educere.
items.cn: educare 意为「养育、抚养、培养」。它是一个相关动词，拉丁作家已把它与 educere 并用。

items.en: English educate appeared in the fifteenth century, first meaning to rear or bring up, then to instruct formally.
items.cn: 英语 educate 在十五世纪出现，最初指养育，后来指正式教导。

items.en: The pair educare and educere are often confused: one stresses nurture, the other the movement out. Both images survive in the English word.
items.cn: educare 与 educere 这对动词常被混淆：一个强调养育，一个强调向外移动。两种意象都留在英语词里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and relationship): the exact first English use is not recorded, and the precise relation between educare and educere is disputed among etymologists.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与关系）：英语最早用例没有精确记录；educare 与 educere 的确切关系在词源学家之间有争议。

note.en: Group one separates the verb from same-root relatives and from a look-alike of a different root; group two holds the everyday verbs for teaching.
note.cn: 第一组把这个动词与同根亲属词、以及一个异源形近词分开；第二组是表示教导的日常动词。

entries.definition: To draw out something hidden or potential; educate develops a person, while educe extracts what is already there.
entries.definitionCN: 把隐藏或潜在之物引出；educate 发展一个人，educe 则提取已经存在之物。

entries.definition: The process or system; the verb names the act that the noun describes.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或制度；动词命名名词所描述的动作。

entries.definition: From in- 'into' plus ducere: to lead someone into a role or knowledge. It shares the leading root but adds entry.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「进入」的成分加 ducere 构成：把某人引入一个角色或知识。它与「引导」同根，却加上「进入」。

entries.definition: From Latin dicare 'to declare', not ducere. It means to devote or inscribe, with no teaching sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dicare「宣告」，并非 ducere；意为奉献或题献，没有教学义。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for helping someone learn; educate is more formal and often implies a longer process.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某人学习的日常动词；educate 更正式，常含较长的过程。

entries.definition: To give explicit directions or lessons; it stresses transmission, while educate can stress development.
entries.definitionCN: 给出明确指令或课程；它强调传递，而 educate 可强调发展。

entries.definition: To develop a specific skill through repeated practice; educate is broader and includes judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 通过反复练习发展特定技能；educate 更宽，包含判断力。

entries.definition: To educate in an institution, or to train someone firmly; it is narrower and often more severe in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 在机构中教育，或严格训练某人；它更窄，语气常更严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ducere means lead, so educate is to lead someone out of not knowing.
normal.cn: ducere 意为引导，所以 educate 是把人从不知中引出来。

normal.en: The two Latin verbs split the work: one rears, the other leads out, and English keeps both images.
normal.cn: 两个拉丁动词分工：一个养育，一个引出，英语保留两种意象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the objects: educate children, educate the public, educate consumers.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示宾语：教育孩子、向公众普及、教育消费者。

normal.en: The reflexive form educates yourself turns the teacher and learner into one person.
normal.cn: 反身形式 educate yourself 把教师与学习者合成一个人。

normal.en: Educe is the bare 'draw out' cousin, with no school attached.
normal.cn: educe 是不带学校的「引出」近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a hand leading a child from a dark room toward a door of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手牵着孩子，从黑屋走向一扇有光的门。

abstract.en: Picture a locked cabinet slowly opened, its contents already inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个上锁的柜子被慢慢打开，里面的东西本来就在。

abstract.en: Picture a question that makes a whole room fall silent and then speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题让整间屋子先静下来，然后开口。

examples.en: The campaign set out to educate voters about the new ballot rules.
examples.cn: 这场运动旨在向选民普及新的投票规则。

examples.en: She was educated at a small school where every class had two teachers.
examples.cn: 她在一所小规模学校受教育，每个班有两名教师。

examples.en: Travel educated his eye for colour long before he studied painting.
examples.cn: 早在他学画之前，旅行就培养了他对颜色的眼光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一丢 凯特」——牵着人往外走，走出无知 → 教育

root: 拉丁 educare「养育、培养」，与 educere「引出」关系密切；educere = 表示「向外」的成分 + ducere「引导」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with school instruction, then move to rearing, public information, skill training, taste, consumer disclosure, self-teaching and finally any movement of a mind out of ignorance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学校教学出发，转到养育、公共普及、技能训练、品味、消费者告知、自学，最后是任何把心智引离无知的移动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leads a child out of a dark room toward a door of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着孩子，从黑暗的屋子走向一扇有光的门。

branches.en: FORMAL AND PRACTICAL: school instruction, then training in a demonstrable skill.
branches.cn: 正式与实践：先是学校教学，再是可演示的技能训练。

branches.en: GROWTH INSIDE A PERSON: rearing of character, then cultivation of taste and judgment.
branches.cn: 一个人内部的成长：品格的养育，再是品味与判断的培养。

branches.en: OUTWARD INFORMATION: the public is informed, and buyers are told what they need to know.
branches.cn: 向外的信息：公众被告知，买家被告知所需之事。

branches.en: TEACHER AND LEARNER AS ONE: self-education turns the verb inward.
branches.cn: 师生合一：自我教育把这个动词转向内部。

branches.en: THE MOVEMENT ITSELF: the widest reading names a mind leaving ignorance.
branches.cn: 移动本身：最宽的读法命名心智离开无知。

intro.en: Educate is a Latin verb of rearing and leading, and English draws a whole school vocabulary from its two related stems.
intro.cn: educate 是一个表示养育与引导的拉丁动词，英语从它两个相关词干取出一整套学校语汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct and introduce; educare gives educate, education, educator and educative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct 与 introduce；educare 衍生 educate、education、educator 与 educative。

items.example: The root supplies the direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供方向。

items.example: Educere is the movement outward.
items.exampleCN: educere 是向外的移动。

items.example: Educare is the care given on the way.
items.exampleCN: educare 是沿途的照料。

items.example: Educate joins direction and care.
items.exampleCN: educate 把方向与照料合在一起。

items.structure: educate plus a suffix of action
items.example: The noun names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名整个过程。

items.structure: educate plus a suffix meaning 'person who acts'
items.example: The agent ending names the person.
items.exampleCN: 执行者词尾命名人。

items.example: Educational labels the field.
items.exampleCN: educational 标出领域。

items.structure: educate plus an adjective ending of tendency
items.example: Educative names the effect.
items.exampleCN: educative 命名效果。

items.meaning: to draw out what is hidden
items.example: Educe is the extraction without the school.
items.exampleCN: educe 是不带学校的提取。

definition_zh: 教育学；教学法；关于教学与学习方法的理论与实践
definition_en: the theory and practice of teaching
core_image: 一位老师把整间教室的桌椅重新摆成半圆，让每个孩子都能看见别人的眼睛，再开始提问
scene: 师范学院的课堂上，学生先设计一堂课，再互相扮演学生，最后拆解刚才每一步为什么有效。The seminar examined pedagogy by having students teach a lesson and then dissect it.
sceneCN: 这里 pedagogy 指关于教学方法的理论与实践（第 1 个义项：教学的艺术与学问）；句意为研讨课让学生先上一堂课，再拆解它，以此来考察教学法。

pos.zh: 教育学；教学法（不可数，指理论、学问或方法体系）
某一教师或某一学科的教学风格与做法

collocations.zh: 评价方式背后的教学观

derivatives.zh: 教师；（贬义）教书匠（由希腊语「护送男孩的家奴」经拉丁与法语进入英语，从照看孩子的人转指教师）
教学法的（由希腊语「教学」词干加表示「属于」的希腊后缀构成，经拉丁与法语进入英语）
教学法的；教育学的（由 pedagogic 加表示「属于」的英语后缀构成）
从教学法角度（由 pedagogical 加表示「方式」的后缀构成）
教学法研究（由 pedagogic 加表示「学问」的后缀构成，指教学法的系统研究）

senses.title: The art and science of teaching
senses.definition: the study and practice of how teaching is done, treated as both a craft and a field of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 对教学如何进行的学问与实践，既被视为技艺，也被视为知识领域
senses.example: The seminar examined pedagogy by having students teach a lesson and then dissect it.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课让学生先上一堂课，再拆解它，以此来考察教学法。
senses.why: The Greek word first named the slave who led a boy to school; the modern word names the study of that leading, now done by teachers themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初命名送男孩上学的家奴；现代词则命名对「引导」这件事的研究，如今由教师自己来做。

senses.title: The theory of instruction
senses.definition: a systematic account of how instruction should be designed and why it works
senses.definitionCN: 关于教学应当如何设计、为何有效的系统论述
senses.example: Her book sets out a pedagogy grounded in how novices actually think.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书提出一种以初学者实际如何思考为基础的教学理论。
senses.why: Theory turns practice into something that can be argued about, tested and taught to new teachers.
senses.whyCN: 理论把实践变成可争论、可检验、可教给新教师的东西。

senses.title: The method or practice of teaching
senses.definition: the concrete choices a teacher makes in a classroom, such as grouping, questioning and pacing
senses.definitionCN: 教师在课堂上做出的具体选择，如分组、提问与节奏
senses.example: His pedagogy changed when he moved the desks into a circle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把课桌摆成圆形后，教学法也随之改变。
senses.why: Here the word is closest to practice: it names what a teacher actually does, not what a journal article recommends.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词最贴近实践：它命名教师实际怎么做，而非期刊论文建议怎么做。

senses.title: Critical pedagogy
senses.definition: an approach that treats teaching as a way of questioning power and inviting students to act
senses.definitionCN: 把教学视为质疑权力、邀请学生行动的一种路径
senses.example: Critical pedagogy asks whose knowledge the textbook leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 批判教育学追问教科书漏掉了谁的知识。
senses.why: A named school within the field, it joins the word to a political commitment rather than to technique alone.
senses.whyCN: 这是领域内部一个有名字的流派，它把教学法与政治承诺结合，而非只与技术结合。

senses.title: The pedagogy of the oppressed
senses.definition: a teaching practice that begins from the experience of the oppressed and aims at their liberation
senses.definitionCN: 从受压迫者的经验出发、以其解放为目标的教学实践
senses.example: The course read the pedagogy of the oppressed alongside folk-school records.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程把受压迫者教育学与民间学校档案并读。
senses.why: The phrase turns teaching into a political act, so pedagogy here is not neutral method but a stance.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把教学变成政治行动，因此这里的教学法不是中立方法，而是一种立场。

senses.title: Subject-specific pedagogy
senses.definition: the particular ways of teaching a subject, such as history pedagogy or mathematics pedagogy
senses.definitionCN: 教授某一学科的特有方式，如历史教学法或数学教学法
senses.example: Mathematics pedagogy has its own debates about symbols and proof.
senses.exampleCN: 数学教学法有自己关于符号与证明的争论。
senses.why: Each discipline has its own ways of making knowledge visible, so the word attaches to the subject.
senses.whyCN: 每门学科都有让知识可见的特有方式，因此这个词会接上具体学科。

senses.title: Curriculum design as pedagogy
senses.titleCN: 课程设计层面的教学法
senses.definition: the arrangement of content, sequence and assessment understood as part of teaching rather than as administration
senses.definitionCN: 把内容、顺序与评价的安排理解为教学的一部分，而非行政事务
senses.example: The new curriculum was praised for its pedagogy, not its list of topics.
senses.exampleCN: 新课程受到称赞的是它的教学安排，而不是主题清单。
senses.why: Design carries teaching: what is placed first and what is tested tells students what kind of learning is expected.
senses.whyCN: 设计本身承载教学：先放什么、考什么，都在告诉学生期待何种学习。

senses.title: Abstract: shaping of learning
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对学习的有意塑造
senses.definition: any deliberate arrangement that shapes how someone learns, inside or outside a classroom
senses.definitionCN: 任何有意安排、塑造某人如何学习的方式，无论课堂内外
senses.example: A good museum label has its own pedagogy.
senses.exampleCN: 一块好的博物馆说明牌也有自己的教学法。
senses.why: At its widest the word names the intention behind an arrangement, not a profession or a syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个词命名安排背后的意图，而非职业或大纲。

intro.en: Pedagogy comes from Greek paidagogia, 'attendance on a boy', built on pais 'child' and agein 'to lead'. The modern sense of theory of teaching is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pedagogy 来自希腊语 paidagogia「照看男孩」，由 pais「孩子」与 agein「引导」构成。现代「教学理论」义要晚得多。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pais, with the stem paid-, meant 'child, boy'. The same stem appears in pediatrics, the care of children.
items.cn: pais 的词干是 paid-，意为「孩子、男孩」。同一词干也出现在 pediatrics（儿科）中。

items.en: Agein meant 'to lead, drive'. It supplies the second half of the word and the idea of guiding someone.
items.cn: agein 意为「引导、驱赶」。它提供这个词的后半段与「引导某人」的意象。

items.en: Paidagogos named the household slave who escorted a boy to school and supervised him on the way. The word named a person, not a theory.
items.cn: paidagogos 指护送男孩上学、沿途照看的家奴。这个词命名的是人，不是理论。

items.en: Paidagogia meant 'attendance on a boy', the work of that slave. In ancient Greek it did not mean the theory of teaching.
items.cn: paidagogia 意为「照看男孩」，是那个家奴的工作。在古希腊语中，它不指教学理论。

items.en: Latin borrowed paedagogus and paedagogia, and French pédagogie carried the word into educational writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 paedagogus 与 paedagogia，法语 pédagogie 把这个词带进教育写作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): English pedagogy is recorded from the sixteenth century, but the modern sense of the theory of teaching became common only later.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语 pedagogy 自十六世纪有记录，但「教学理论」这一现代义后来才通行。

note.en: Group one separates the word from its relative for the teacher and from two Greek look-alikes; group two holds the near names for teaching as a field.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与指教师的亲属词、以及两个希腊语形近词分开；第二组是把教学作为领域的近邻名称。

entries.definition: The teacher; the noun for the person, while pedagogy names the theory or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 教师；这个名词指人，而 pedagogy 指理论或实践。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching methods; the adjective describes what pedagogy names.
entries.definitionCN: 与教学方法有关的；形容词描述 pedagogy 所命名的东西。

entries.definition: From pais 'child' plus iatreia 'healing'; it shares the child stem but has nothing to do with teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pais「孩子」加 iatreia「治疗」构成；它共享「孩子」词干，却与教学无关。

entries.definition: From dēmos 'people' plus agein 'lead': leading the people by appeal to emotion. It shares agein but not pais.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dēmos「人民」加 agein「引导」构成：以情绪诉求引导民众。它共享 agein，却不共享 pais。

entries.definition: The everyday name for the activity; pedagogy adds theory, method and reflection.
entries.definitionCN: 这项活动的日常名称；pedagogy 加上理论、方法与反思。

entries.definition: The act of delivering lessons or directions; it stresses transmission more than pedagogy does.
entries.definitionCN: 传递课程或指令的行为；它比 pedagogy 更强调传递。

entries.definition: The study of teaching methods, from Greek didaskein 'to teach'; it overlaps with pedagogy but is often narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 对教学方法的研究，来自希腊语 didaskein「教」；与 pedagogy 重叠，但通常更窄。

entries.definition: The broad process and system of educating; pedagogy is the teaching side of it, not the whole institution.
entries.definitionCN: 教育的广义过程与制度；pedagogy 是其中教学的一面，而非整个制度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real Greek words and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的希腊词与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pais means child, so pedagogy begins with the young person being led.
normal.cn: pais 意为孩子，所以 pedagogy 从被引导的年轻人开始。

normal.en: Agein means lead, so the second half is the act of guiding, not filling.
normal.cn: agein 意为引导，所以后半段是引导的动作，不是填充。

normal.en: The ancient paidagogos was a slave escort, which is why the word first named a person rather than a method.
normal.cn: 古代的 paidagogos 是护送的家奴，所以这个词最初命名人，而非方法。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the schools: critical pedagogy, subject pedagogy, classroom pedagogy.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出流派：批判教育学、学科教学法、课堂教学法。

normal.en: Pediatrics shares pais but not agein, so it is about children's health, not teaching.
normal.cn: pediatrics 共享 pais 却不共享 agein，所以它关乎儿童健康，与教学无关。

abstract.en: Picture a room rearranged into a half circle so every child can see every other child's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子被摆成半圆，让每个孩子都能看见别人的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a lesson taken apart on a table like a clock, each step laid beside the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一堂课像钟表一样被拆在桌上，每一步都摆在下一步旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp carried ahead of a small figure on a dark road to school.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯在暗路上走在一个小身影前面，通往学校。

examples.en: The department treats pedagogy as a research field, not as a set of tricks.
examples.cn: 这个系把教学法当作研究领域，而非一套窍门。

examples.en: Her pedagogy gives students time to be wrong before they are corrected.
examples.cn: 她的教学法给学生留出犯错的时间，再加以纠正。

examples.en: The report compares the pedagogy of online and face-to-face courses.
examples.cn: 报告比较在线课程与面授课程的教学法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派达 够 吉」——牵着孩子走向学堂的那门学问 → 教学法

root: 希腊 pais「孩子」+ agein「引导」→ paidagogos「护送男孩的家奴」→ paidagogia「照看男孩」；现代「教学理论」义为后起。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with teaching as a craft and a field, then move to theory, classroom practice, critical schools, liberation, subject methods, curriculum design and finally any deliberate shaping of learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把教学看作技艺与领域，再转到理论、课堂实践、批判流派、解放、学科方法、课程设计，最后是任何对学习的有意塑造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp carried ahead of a child on the road to school, then the same road studied by teachers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯在孩子上学的路上走在前头，随后这条路由教师来研究。

branches.en: CRAFT AND CLASSROOM: teaching as knowledge, then as the concrete choices made in a room.
branches.cn: 技艺与课堂：教学作为知识，再作为课堂中的具体选择。

branches.en: THEORY: instruction explained systematically so that it can be argued and tested.
branches.cn: 理论：对教学作系统解释，使其可被争论与检验。

branches.en: CRITICAL AND LIBERATING: named schools that make teaching a political stance.
branches.cn: 批判与解放：有名字的流派，把教学变成政治立场。

branches.en: SUBJECT AND SEQUENCE: methods specific to a discipline, and design as a form of teaching.
branches.cn: 学科与顺序：特定学科的方法，以及作为教学形式的设计。

branches.en: THE INTENTION: any arrangement that deliberately shapes how someone learns.
branches.cn: 意图：任何有意塑造某人如何学习的安排。

intro.en: Pedagogy is Greek from top to bottom: a child, a leader and the slave who walked between them.
intro.cn: pedagogy 从头到尾都是希腊语：一个孩子、一位引导者，以及走在两者之间的家奴。

latinIntro.en: Greek pais and agein build paidagogos and paidagogia; English adds pedagogy, pedagogue and pedagogical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 pais 与 agein 构成 paidagogos 与 paidagogia；英语再加 pedagogy、pedagogue 与 pedagogical。

definition_zh: 教学法的；教育学的；与教学方法和教育理论有关的
definition_en: relating to teaching methods or the theory of education
core_image: 教案的页边写满小字，每一处停顿、每一个提问顺序都被标出来，像给一堂课画的施工图
scene: 新老师把同一段课文设计成三种提问顺序，请同事观察哪一种更能让学生开口。The new teacher treated the lesson plan as a pedagogical experiment rather than a script.
sceneCN: 这里 pedagogical 指与教学方法和教育理论有关的（第 1 个义项：教学法层面的）；句意为这位新老师把教案当作一次教学法实验，而不是照本宣科的脚本。

pos.zh: 教学法的；教育学的；与教学方法有关的
带有教学意图的；为促进学习而设计的

derivatives.zh: 教育学；教学法（由希腊语 paidagogia「照看男孩」经拉丁与法语进入英语）
教师；教书匠（由希腊语 paidagogos「护送男孩的家奴」经拉丁进入英语）
教学法的（由 pedagogy 的词干加表示「属于」的希腊后缀构成）
